We are seeking an experienced **NPI Director North America - Solutions** to provide regional leadership for New Product Introduction across North America, covering the relevant manufacturing sites and Design Center capabilities. The role translates business and customer priorities into a coherent NPI strategy, governance model and project portfolio, ensuring that new products move from concept to stable commercialization with the required quality, cost, timing, compliance and manufacturability. The role aligns Commercial, Global Design Center, NPI, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement and Manufacturing and develops the capabilities required for consistent execution across sites..

**Key Responsibilities:**

**NPI strategy and governance**

* Translate the global NPI strategy into the North American operating model, stage-gate governance, priorities and decision routines, aligned with the Global Accounts and Global Design Center Director.
* Own the North American NPI portfolio and facilitate prioritization, resource allocation, escalation and trade-off decisions across customer programs and manufacturing sites in the region.
* Implement and continuously improve common global standards, templates, performance measures and management routines for product development, prototyping, design transfer, validation and industrialization.
* Ensure early NPI and Design Center involvement in strategic customer opportunities and new product concepts.

**Portfolio delivery and industrialization**

* Oversee major and complex NPI programs from concept through commercialization and stable production handover.
* Ensure projects have clear business cases, requirements, milestones, risks, accountabilities and readiness criteria.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, cost engineering, value engineering and manufacturability reviews before production commitment.
* Ensure product concepts are technically feasible, compliant, financially viable and transferable across the relevant North American manufacturing network, while ensuring effective transfer to or from other regions when required.
* Lead executive-level reviews of portfolio status, critical risks, capacity constraints and recovery plans.

**Cross-functional and customer leadership**

* Act as the senior NPI interface for strategic customer programs and align customer expectations with operational capabilities.
* Build strong collaboration across Commercial, Business Development, Design, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain and Manufacturing.
* Coordinate North American and global resources to resolve cross-functional issues and accelerate decision making.
* Promote disciplined change control and transparent communication throughout the development and industrialization process.

**Capability and team leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the North American NPI organization with teams in Seattle, Dallas and East-Longmeadow, including regional managers, project leaders and specialist resources.
* Build project management, product industrialization, risk management and technical problem-solving capabilities.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**WHY DO WE NEED YOU?**

The Senior Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, efficient, and profitable operation of our CertainTeed Roofing manufacturing facility in Peachtree City. Reporting to the Senior Director of Regional Operations, this role provides overall leadership for safety, quality, production, cost, delivery, people development, and sustainability performance.

You will set the vision and culture for the site, align daily operations with business strategy, and lead continuous improvement and long term plant performance. Success in this role requires sound judgment, strong business and people leadership, and the ability to balance workforce engagement, customer expectations, regulatory compliance, and community responsibility.

 **IS THIS JOB FOR YOU?**

**What you will do:**

* Lead all aspects of plant operations, including safety, production, maintenance, quality, logistics, engineering, and environmental performance.
* Build and sustain a strong safety culture where health and safety are integrated into daily decisions and operations.
* Deliver plant performance goals across safety, quality, service, cost, productivity, and profitability.
* Own the plant operating budget, forecasting, cost management, and long range planning.
* Drive continuous improvement through Lean Manufacturing, reliability, process optimization, problem solving, and operational excellence.
* Lead change initiatives and translate business strategy into actionable plant priorities and measurable results.
* Build and develop a high performing leadership team through coaching, feedback, succession planning, and employee development.
* Partner cross functionally with Sales, Supply Chain, R&D, Product Management, and other key stakeholders to support customer and business needs.
* Provide leadership for major capital projects and other strategic plant initiatives.

**What you bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent experience, required.
* 10+ years of progressive production or operations management experience.
* 5 to 7 years of experience at the Production Manager or Plant Superintendent level preferred.
* Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, or Operations Management preferred.
* Strong knowledge of production planning, scheduling, supply chain, budgeting, forecasting, and cost control.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, WCM, or similar continuous improvement methodologies.
* Knowledge of quality management systems, equipment reliability, process optimization, OSHA requirements, and safety practices.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem solving, and change management skills.
* Ability to travel domestically approximately 20% of the time.

 
**A LITTLE MORE ABOUT US**

Through the responsible development of innovative and sustainable building products, CertainTeed, headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, has helped shape the building products industry for more than 110 years. Founded in 1904 as General Roofing Manufacturing Company, the company’s slogan, “Quality Made Certain, Satisfaction Guaranteed,” inspired the name CertainTeed. Today, CertainTeed is a leading North American brand of exterior and interior building products, including roofing, siding, trim, insulation, drywall, and ceilings. CertainTeed is a subsidiary of Saint-Gobain, one of the world’s largest and oldest building products companies.

 **LEGAL STATEMENT**

Saint-Gobain provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws. Saint-Gobain is an equal opportunity employer of individuals with disabilities and supports the hiring of veterans.

Applicants for roles based in Washington state or remote roles that would be worked from Washington state are encouraged to direct any concerns regarding the state’s Pay Transparency laws to the SGNA HR Compliance team at SGNA\_HR\_Compliance@saint-gobain.com.

 **BENEFITS IN JOINING US**

Saint-Gobain aims to deliver a comprehensive Total Rewards package that supports employees’ wellbeing and helps improve daily life for employees and their families. Be Well. Be You brings together inclusive programs and meaningful resources that support physical, emotional, financial, and social wellbeing. Employees have flexibility to choose the benefits that best fit their individual needs.

Retirement and protection

* Company provided life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment insurance, and short term disability
* Voluntary employee and dependent life insurance, long term disability, critical illness insurance, and accident insurance

Additional benefits

**Job Description**

**This role is fully remote and must be located within the 50 U.S. states. Standard working hours are in Eastern Timezone. Semi-annual travel may be required to a Devoted office for on-site work.**

**A bit about this role:**

At Devoted, our mission is to dramatically improve the health and well-being of our members by treating each of them like family. Devoted is growing at an incredible pace, and we are thrilled to welcome and serve every new member who joins us. This growth demands that our Utilization Management (UM) operation must scale and evolve without ever losing sight of the people at the center of every authorization.

We believe UM done right means decisions that are correct, fair, and fast, delivered through a frictionless process and with heart. Behind every request is a member waiting on care and a provider working to deliver it. UM is hard, but the challenge doesn’t exempt us from our mission.

We are seeking a curious, operationally minded leader to serve as Director, Utilization Management Operations. Reporting to the Vice President of Health Services, you will lead the teams behind our administrative work: a large onshore and offshore team of UM Administrative Coordinators who manage intake, outreach, notifications, and follow-up. You will also hold dotted-line accountability for monitoring and ensuring the success of our Part B medical authorization turnaround times (TAT).

This role is for someone who is energized by a complex process: someone who wants to unravel it, reimagine it, and lead the build of something simpler, faster, and more consistent. You will have significant influence over the roadmap for Orinoco, our internal technology platform, and an integrated AI engine to put to work. This role will help pave the way towards realizing the next generation of our UM program, driving improvements in effectiveness, efficiency, and experience for our members and provider partners.

**Your Responsibilities and Impact will include**:

* **SLA & Timeliness Ownership:** Own SLA performance for the administrative steps that support authorization review across UM, delivering consistent, predictable performance at a meaningfully lower cost. Hold dotted-line accountability for Part B medical authorization turnaround times (TAT), partnering with the clinical leaders of that team to monitor performance, surface risks early, and remove administrative barriers to on-time decisions.
* **Process Reimagination:** Map our administrative processes end to end, including auth intake, requests for additional clinical information, facility census checks, member and provider notifications, and member follow-up, and lead their redesign for speed, consistency, and simplicity.
* **Technology & AI Leadership:** Partner with Product and Engineering to shape the Orinoco roadmap so that process and technology evolve together. Put our integrated AI tools to work to remove manual effort, so our administrative capacity no longer has to grow at the same rate as our membership.
* **Build for Measurement:** Design processes that are highly measurable and transparent by default. Partner with Data Science to define and monitor the KPIs that matter, including timeliness, cost per authorization, quality, and provider experience, and use them to drive decisions and continuous improvement.
* **People & Vendor Leadership:** Lead and develop a team that includes approximately 50 onshore UM Administrative Coordinators and their leaders. Manage our offshore vendor partnership, which supports more than 250 administrative team members, holding it to clear performance standards while building a shared culture of ownership and care.
* **Provider & Member Experience:** Partner with the Provider Network team to understand what providers and facilities need from this process, and build it in. Design every touchpoint, from outreach to notifications to follow-up, with the humans on the other end in mind.
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Work closely with the Senior Director of UM, who owns end-to-end authorization performance, along with the UM Medical Directors, Compliance, Provider Network, Data Science, and Engineering teams to keep the operation aligned and consistently audit-ready.

**Required skills and experience:**

* **Mission & Heart:** A genuine commitment to treating members like family, and a belief that operational excellence and empathy belong together.
* **Proven Operator at Scale:** A track record of leading high-volume operations that deliver consistent SLA performance.
* **Builder Mindset:** Experience taking a complex, multi-step process apart and leading the build of a simpler, more scalable one, rather than only maintaining what exists. You are naturally curious and ask why a step exists before deciding how to improve it.
* **Metrics-Oriented:** You build for measurement, are comfortable working deep in the workflows and the data, and use both to drive decisions and hold teams and partners accountable.
* **Technology & AI Curiosity:** Experience partnering with product and engineering teams, and genuine excitement about using AI-enabled tools to transform how work gets done.
* **Vendor Management:** Experience managing vendor partners against clear performance and quality standards.
* **Communication:** Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex problems into actionable updates for leadership and stakeholders.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree required.

**Desired skills and experience**:

* **Healthcare Operations:** Experience in payer operations, utilization management, claims, provider revenue cycle, or a similar high-volume healthcare environment. Prior UM experience is not required.
* **Medicare Advantage Familiarity:** Understanding of Medicare Advantage operations and CMS requirements.
* **Advanced Degree:** MBA or advanced degree in health administration or finance is a plus.
* MBA or advanced degree in health administration or finance is a plus.

#LI-DS1

***Salary range:*** $182,000 - 247,000 / year

The pay range listed for this position is the range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of the posting. Once the interview process begins, your talent partner will provide additional information on the compensation for the role, along with additional information on our total rewards package. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.

Our Total Rewards package includes:

* Employer sponsored health, dental and vision plan with low or no premium
* Generous paid time off
* $100 monthly mobile or internet stipend
* Stock options for all employees
* Bonus eligibility for all roles excluding Director and above; Commission eligibility for Sales roles
* Parental leave program
* 401K program
* And more....

* *Our total rewards package is for full time employees only. Intern and Contract positions are not eligible.*

Founded in 2017, Devoted Health is on a mission to dramatically improve the health and well-being of older Americans by caring for everyone like they are family, and that includes our employees. Our robust and seamlessly integrated care platform merges advanced data and AI access with world-class clinical and service experiences to create a member experience that is unlike the industry norm. To continue building upon our mission, we want to bring together those who share our values, embrace change and advancement, and are enthusiastic about where we're going — all the while bringing their own unique qualities, experiences, and expertise, in hopes of further changing the healthcare experience.

Devoted is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to a safe and supportive work environment in which all employees have the opportunity to participate and contribute to the success of the business. We value diversity and collaboration. Individuals are respected for their skills, experience, and unique perspectives. This commitment is embodied in Devoted’s Code of Conduct, our company values and the way we do business.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, the Company does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy status, marital status, national origin, disability, age, sexual orientation, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, or any other factor prohibited by law. Our management team is dedicated to this policy with respect to recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, employee activities and general treatment during employment.

 

We have been made aware of instances of fraudulent job postings and/or fraudulent recruiting activity by individuals purporting to represent Devoted Health. These fraudulent schemes often seek monetary contributions or payments from job seekers (such as for “start up costs” or “equipment”), or seek to collect sensitive personal information. These job postings and offers are **NOT**authorized by Devoted Health and Devoted is not responsible for fraudulent offers, personal information that you may have disclosed, or payments made to third parties purporting to represent Devoted. We have reported this matter and are cooperating with law enforcement agencies. Devoted Health will never ask for financial commitment or contribution from a candidate at any stage of the recruitment process.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Job Title: Plant Manager**

**Job Type: On-Site**

**Location: Orange, CA**

**Reporting to: VP of Manufacturing**

**Company Overview**

FXI is a leading producer of foam innovation in the Bedding, Furniture, Industrial, Home & Office, Healthcare, and Transportation markets. We have made it our mission to provide tailored solutions that delight our customers and consumers. With our corporate headquarters, high-tech research and development facility, and multiple manufacturing locations in North America, FXI has built a culture of innovation and achievement that is recognized by customers, suppliers and peers. Our products include finished goods, sub-assemblies, services, and raw materials for OEMs, fabricators, and retailers. You will find FXI's foam innovations inside, around, and under yourself in countless applications. Everywhere foam goes, FXI's innovations lead the way! Won't you join us?

**Job Overview:**

Reporting to the Manufacturing Vice President, the Plant Manager plans, directs, and coordinates the operations of the plant. The Plant Manager has leadership responsibility to assure compliance with all government and company policies and procedures. This position will also be responsible for facility production goals and objectives. Following FXI's Vision, Mission and Values, the Plant Manager is to develop a well-trained and motivated staff with emphasis on plant safety and employee engagement.

**Responsibilities:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Chemical, or related discipline) preferred.

* Direct and coordinate plant operations in strict compliance with all state and federal laws, regulations, corporate policies and procedures
* Responsible for achieving all facility business goals including, but not limited to, the areas of safety, quality, production, reliability and P&L.

* Maintain a clean and safe plant; incorporate a 5S culture for conducting all work activities.

* Develop and foster a high‑performing, well‑trained, and motivated workforce by assessing current skill sets and aligning talent development with the plant's future growth, vision, and manufacturing excellence across all functions.

* Lead the development, implementation, and governance of plant performance metrics and KPIs to monitor progress toward site objectives and drive continuous improvement.

* Conduct and assure all required employee development and performance reviews are completed to promote individual continuous improvement per the required corporate schedule.

* Attend scheduled corporate training and meetings. Need to be a key leader moving the company forward to meet strategic and business plan objectives.
* Ensures that all plant assets are properly managed, safeguarded, and secure.

* Develop, submit for approval, and implement approved Capital Projects as required to meet facility strategic plans and business needs.

* Develop and ensure management systems are in place to monitor plant output, cuts / yields and scrap to ensure efficient resource utilization and initiate corrective action as required.

* Establish and maintain a positive community relationship.

**Qualifications:**

* 10 years of prior experience in a manufacturing environment
* Prior experience as Production / Operations Manager.
* Strong interpersonal, problem solving and leadership skills with the ability to lead a team motivate the group and manage a diverse workforce.
* Excellent, engaging communicator; able to set measurable goals and expectations and hold team members accountable for results

* Demonstrated experience and working knowledge of Lean Manufacturing principles and structured problem‑solving tools (e.g., 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, Root Cause Analysis, A3, 5 Whys) to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence.

* Action-oriented and eager to drive programs through to completion. Able to deal with pressures and timelines inherent in a fast-paced company
* Ability to quickly assess the situation at the plant and have an impact on the direction of improvements
* Ability to function as a strong leader, bringing the Operations perspective while promoting cross-functional horizontal alignment to achieve key company goals
* Hands-on leader who contributes to overall business strategy and issues, works well as part of the leadership team, and is focused upon achieving results
* Team player and coach who will promote cooperation among employees in the organization and an environment of employee engagement
* Possess the confidence and presence to be able to deal effectively with external customers, vendors, and all levels within the organization
* Strong, self-confident, decisive leader with excellent listening skills, emotional maturity, and ability to adapt to a rapidly changing environment

**Our Commitment to a Diverse Workforce:** FXI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. FXI does not discriminate in employment matters on the basis of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, military service eligibility, veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or based on any individual's membership in any group or class protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. We support workplace diversity. We strongly believe that diversity contributes to a broader collective perspective that will consistently lead to a better company and better products. We are working hard to increase the diversity of our team wherever we can.

***We are interested in every*** ***qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.***

FXI is not accepting unsolicited assistance from search firms for this employment opportunity. Please, no phone calls or emails. All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee at FXI via-email, the Internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written search agreement in place for this position will be deemed the sole property of FXI. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by FXI as a result of the referral or through other means.

The Senior Director, Commercial Manufacturing & Operations is Olema’s senior leader accountable for building, scaling and governing the commercial manufacturing and supply platform for palazestrant.

Provide business and operational oversight of commercial DS and DP manufacturing, partnering with CMC Technical, Quality and Regulatory on registrational readiness, PPQ, process validation and the transition to commercial supply.
Coordinate batch disposition with Quality and the release of finished goods to the 3PL.

We expect top-line data from OPERA-01, our ongoing Phase 3 trial of palazestrant as a monotherapy in patients with second- or third-line ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (MBC), in Q1 2027 which, if positive, could lead to our first potential approval and commercial launch in 2028.
Commercial Supply Strategy & Launch Readiness

We expect top-line data from OPERA-01, our ongoing Phase 3 trial of palazestrant as a monotherapy in patients with second- or third-line ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (MBC), in Q1 2027 which, if positive, could lead to our first potential approval and commercial launch in 2028.

We recently presented encouraging Phase 1 monotherapy data from this program across multiple solid tumor types, are advancing patient enrollment in the ongoing combination arms in MBC, and expect to initiate a Phase 1 study of OP-3136 in combination with Bayer’s darolutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer by the end of this year.
Strategic and hands-on: shapes the commercial supply platform and does the daily work a lean, build-from-scratch organization requires.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
The Director of Quality Engineering – Automation & Performance is the senior technical, delivery, and practice leader for iLAB U.S. Automation and Performance Testing. The role is accountable for the day-to-day management of U.S. engineering initiatives and resources, while also providing hands-on consulting leadership for strategic clients.

This leader defines the practice strategy, architecture, standards, delivery assurance, reusable solutions, and capability roadmap for Automation and Performance Testing. Working as part of a global delivery organization, they combine technical credibility, client leadership, people management, and commercial judgment to deliver measurable quality outcomes, strengthen service offerings, and build scalable engineering capability.

* Own the day-to-day delivery, prioritization, staffing, allocation, utilization, performance, and technical direction of all iLAB U.S. Automation and Performance Testing initiatives and resources.
* Define and evolve Automation and Performance Testing strategies, capability roadmaps, service offerings, architectures, standards, frameworks, methods, tools, reusable accelerators, and intellectual property.
* Oversee technical assurance across high-impact deliveries, including solution architecture, automation and performance engineering design, CI/CD integration, AI-enabled engineering guardrails, test-data readiness, and environment readiness.
* Lead critical client-facing activities, including technical discovery, project kickoffs, solutioning workshops, executive presentations, steering reviews, escalations, and project recovery.
* Serve as the senior technical escalation point for complex or at-risk engagements and personally provide architecture, assessment, technical review, troubleshooting, and recovery leadership until delivery is stabilized.
* Lead the technical development and review of RFIs, RFPs, proposals, SOWs, estimates, staffing models, assumptions, deliverables, risks, acceptance criteria, and service commitments
* Establish and oversee practical engineering governance, including quality gates, code and architecture reviews, documentation standards, source-control practices, repository security, and technical approval processes.
* Define and guide responsible, value-focused uses of AI within Automation and Performance Testing, including test design assistance, script development and maintenance, results analysis, defect insight, and knowledge retrieval, while applying company security, privacy, data-handling, and human-review requirements
* Hire, coach, develop, and retain engineering managers, architects, principal engineers, and technical specialists; establish competency expectations, career paths, succession plans, and backup coverage for critical capabilities.
* Collaborate with global delivery leaders to align technical standards, share reusable assets and expertise, and support other geographies with strategic client and delivery needs.
* Partner with Sales, Professional Services, Operations, Finance, and Talent Management on capacity planning, forecasting, utilization, delivery margin and growth opportunities.
* Represent iLAB as a Quality Engineering thought leader through conferences, industry events, client advisory councils, publications, demonstrations, and market-facing content.

* At least 15 years of progressive experience in Quality Engineering, including senior leadership of complex Automation and Performance Testing solutions, consulting engagements, engineering teams, and CxO-level client relationships
* Deep knowledge of Automation and Performance Testing strategies, architectures, frameworks, tools, workload models, execution practices, analysis, reporting, and integration with modern software delivery pipelines
* Experience leading technical delivery across multiple clients, programs, or business units, including distributed teams and critical project recovery.
* Working knowledge of CI/CD integration, testability, observability, test-data and environment readiness, cloud delivery, and AI-assisted engineering practices.
* Proven people leadership, including resource planning, coaching, performance management, prioritization, utilization, and organizational development.
* Strong consulting and client-advisory skills, with the ability to translate business needs into practical technical solutions and delivery plans.
* Experience shaping proposals, SOWs, estimates, resource models, and commercial commitments.
* Sound understanding of consulting engagement economics, including forecasting, utilization, margin, cost-to-serve, and measurable client outcomes.
* A mature, politically astute leadership style; calm in a crisis, able to lead by influence and example, with excellent written and oral communication.
* Willing and able to travel interstate and occasionally internationally for critical client-facing initiatives, project kickoffs, workshops, presentations, escalations, and recovery efforts.
* Demonstrated experience in a Quality Assurance, Quality Engineering, Automation, or Performance Testing consulting or professional-services organization.
* Experience across the consulting lifecycle and multi-country delivery teams; relevant industry expertise and advanced professional certifications are beneficial.

**You’ve discovered something special. A company that cares. Cares about leading the way in construction, engineering, manufacturing and renewable energy. Cares about redefining how energy is designed, applied and consumed. Cares about thoughtfully growing to meet market demands. And as “one of the Healthiest 100 Workplaces in America” is focused on the mind/body/soul of team members through our** **Culture of Care** **.**

The Plant Manager role is strategic and people-driven and will lead all aspects of manufacturing operations within our facility. This role is responsible for driving performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team culture. The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in Lean Manufacturing, a commitment to developing people, and a passion for operational excellence.

As Plant Manager, you will play a key role in executing our Lean Operating System and ensuring alignment with company goals and values, including our key behaviors of: People First, We Work Together, and We Learn and Grow.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS**

Education: Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Business, Operations Management or a related field. (Master’s preferred). Certification in Lean, Six Sigma, or similar experience preferred.

Experience: 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including 3+ years as a Plant or Operations Manager, with a proven track record of implementing and sustaining Lean Manufacturing principles. Brings strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills, along with the ability to lead through influence, set clear expectations, and hold teams accountable. Deep knowledge of manufacturing processes, safety regulations, and quality systems, with a consistent focus on driving operational excellence. Experienced in identifying process improvement opportunities and implementing safer, more efficient practices across operations. Demonstrated success in managing, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams, and skilled in using the Choosing By Advantages (CBA) decision-making methodology. ERP systems experience is preferred.

Travel: Up to 15% depending on business needs

Work Schedule: This position works between the hours of 6 am and 6 pm, Monday through Friday. However, work may be performed at any time on any day of the week to meet business needs.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide leadership and vision for plant operations, driving a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement
* Inspire and develop leaders across Production, Materials, Quality and Engineering.
* Delivering key business results in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee engagement.
* Drive Operational Excellence through Lean tools, systems thinking and problem-solving.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Engineering, HR, Finance, and Supply Chain to support business objectives
* Champion our Key Behaviors: People First, We Work Together, and We Learn and Grow.
* Monitor KPIs and take proactive steps to improve efficiency, reduce waste, and drive customer satisfaction
* Ensure compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and safety standards
* Act as a change agent—driving strategic initiatives and fostering a culture of ownership, learning, and innovation
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned.

 The LADS SBU is seeking an Execution Production Chief Engineer (P5) to support technical execution for the LTAMDS (Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense Sensor) Production program. LTAMDS is a Raytheon franchise program delivering next‑generation radar capability with 360‑degree coverage to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic weapons. This role reports to the Production Chief Engineer and supports the LTAMDS Sub‑Strategic Business Unit (SSBU) Office of the Chief Engineer (OCE).  Experience leading engineering teams or task forces and supporting proposals or EAC activities.
 Experience managing or influencing work associated with multi‑million‑dollar budgets.

postingQuotes: The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.

* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical

* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.

* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.

* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.

### **Location**

On-site in San Francisco, California, five days per week. Relocation within the United States is supported.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Airlite Plastics is a premier, privately held, family-owned manufacturer headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Our family style and personal culture is what makes Airlite an amazing place to grow and build a successful career. Airlite’s company values of unquestionable integrity and respect and appreciation for each other are at the core of our success! These values set a strong foundation to build on where we can ‘wow’ our customers with innovative products and sustainable solutions and continuously improve our processes and efficiencies.

 

Our product lines include rigid plastic containers and lids for food packaging and cosmetics, dry powder scoops, plastic drink cups, shipping containers, industrial strength insulated concrete forms (ICF) and sustainable permeable paving systems. As pioneers in our industry, focused on sustainable solutions, we strive to provide our customers with top-notch service and quality, which aligns with our award-winning products.

 

As Airlite continues to grow and expand, we are excited to add new roles across our organization to support increasing customer demand and future innovation. This is an exciting time to join our team and be part of a company investing in people, technology, and long-term success.

 

**How would you contribute?**

This role is a contributing member of our team located in Nazareth, PA. As a Director of Operations you are a key to continued growth and success of Airlite. The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for manufacturing operations across assigned Airlite Locations. This role is responsible for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering and ensures operational strategies, resources, and priorities are aligned with business objectives.

This role will drive operational excellence through strong leadership, development of site leadership teams, continuous improvement, effective use of performance metrics, and disciplined execution. A key focus of this position is building leadership capability throughout the organization by coaching and developing managers and supervisors as the operations continue to grow and evolve. The Director will balance consistent operational expectations across locations while recognizing the unique needs and autonomy of each facility.

**Essential Duties:**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering across the Nazareth and Lakeville facilities.

* Lead, coach, and develop operational leaders, strengthening leadership capability, accountability, decision-making, and succession readiness throughout the organization.

* Establish operational priorities, goals, and KPIs and use performance data to drive accountability and continuous improvement.

* Ensure manufacturing operations consistently achieve objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, productivity, efficiency, and cost.

* Partner with site leadership to develop and execute operational plans that support business growth, capacity requirements, equipment needs, and organizational objectives.

* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve manufacturing processes, equipment reliability, labor effectiveness, throughput, and overall operational performance.

* Provide leadership for capital projects, equipment installations, process improvements, and other operational initiatives in partnership with Engineering and Maintenance.

* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing, and leadership needs and develop teams capable of supporting current operations and future growth.

* Promote consistency and sharing of best practices between facilities while allowing each operation to respond effectively to its specific business and manufacturing needs.

* Partner cross-functionally with Quality, Supply Chain, Safety, Human Resources, Finance, Sales, Customer Service, and other functions to resolve issues and achieve business objectives.

* Develop and manage operational budgets, forecasts, capital requirements, and resource plans in alignment with financial and strategic objectives.

* Foster a culture of safety, accountability, collaboration, employee development, continuous improvement, and operational excellence while exemplifying Airlite's Core Values and servant leadership principles.

* Other duties as assigned.

 

**Do you have what it takes?** Airlite Plastics is a versatile employer; complacency is not one of our strengths! We work hard each day to ensure that equipment efficiency and customer satisfaction never leave our line of sight. Successful candidates for the role will possess the following:

 

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including significant responsibility for manufacturing operations.
* 5+ years of experience leading managers and/or senior operational leaders.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple operational functions such as Production, Maintenance, and Engineering.
* Experience leading operations across multiple facilities or business units strongly preferred.
* Experience with capital planning, operational budgeting, continuous improvement, and manufacturing performance management.
* Plastics manufacturing, injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing experience preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop managers and emerging leaders.
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to understand the impact of operational decisions on overall business performance.
* Ability to effectively lead across multiple facilities, balancing consistent operational expectations with the unique needs of each location.
* Capability to solve complex problems, utilizing strong critical thinking and decision-making skills
* Superior organizational skills and the ability to assemble resources needed to orchestrate multiple projects/activities and accomplish goals
* Model a collaborative leadership style with the ability to build partnerships and influence others into action
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills
* Outstanding presentation and facilitation skills
* Excellent interpersonal skills and consultative approach; tactful in dealing with people at all levels
* Strong sense of urgency, self-motivated and positive
* Flexible and adaptable; able to work in ambiguous situations
* Ability to actively lead change initiatives
* Display highest ethical standards
* Maintain the utmost level of confidentiality in dealing with sensitive information
* Detail oriented, with the ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; stand; walk; use hand dexterity to operate office equipment including computer keyboards; reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to moving mechanical parts. The noise level in the office work environment is typically quiet; when visiting the production floor, the noise level may be loud.

 

**Our Core Values Drive Us!**

 

* Do you conduct yourself with unquestionable integrity?

* Do you demonstrate respect and appreciation for those around you?

* Are you innovative and strive to challenge the status quo?

* Do you strive for continuous improvement and to deliver the “wow” factor?

* Do you care about environmentally sustainable solutions?

* Do you take meaning and pride in a job well done?

 

**What’s in it for you?** ***As a Full-Time employee, you will be eligible for the following benefits:***

 

* Health, dental and vision insurance

* Company paid life insurance

* Company paid short term disability

* Generous 401k match

* Generous Time Off

* Annual company activities

**JOB DESCRIPTION** 
 
 

Step into a leadership role, where your management skills will drive strategic risk and compliance initiatives. Embrace the opportunity to enhance your leadership capabilities and make a meaningful impact on the future of risk management and control testing. 
 
As a **Compliance and Operations Risk Test Director** in the Testing Center of Excellence, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the testing strategy across various business lines, ensuring alignment with regulatory and firm requirements. Your expertise in risk management and control testing will be instrumental in identifying and mitigating risks, thereby enhancing compliance and operational risk management. You will be expected to make independent decisions that significantly impact operations and financial management, while also leading large teams and managing service delivery. Your proficiency in problem-solving, decision-making, and resource optimization will be key in driving results that accelerate our business objectives. Your role will also involve fostering strong relationships with stakeholders, interpreting regulatory requirements, and effectively communicating risk reports to various management levels. 
 
**Job responsibilities**

* Lead the development and implementation of comprehensive testing strategies across various business lines, ensuring alignment with regulatory and firm requirements.
* Oversee complex testing initiatives, utilizing advanced knowledge in risk management and control testing to identify and mitigate unmitigated risks.
* Make independent, strategic decisions that significantly impact operations, financial management, and compliance, based on in-depth analysis and expert judgment.
* Foster strong relationships with senior stakeholders, interpreting regulatory requirements and effectively communicating risk reports to various management levels.
* Manage large teams, setting professional standards, and ensuring efficient service delivery, while also contributing to the longer-term plans for the area to fit within broader functional and organization strategy.

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* 10 years of experience in leading and implementing comprehensive testing strategies in a financial institution.
* Proven track record in managing large teams, setting professional standards, and ensuring efficient service delivery.
* Demonstrated expertise in interpreting and applying regulatory requirements within the context of risk management and control testing.
* Advanced proficiency in utilizing risk dashboards to provide SMART risk reporting, communications, and presentations for various forums and management levels.
* Expertise in resource optimization, with a focus on efficiently leveraging allocated people, money, and technologies to plan, schedule, and progress project and program initiatives.

**ABOUT US** 
 
 

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans

 
 
**ABOUT THE TEAM** 
 
 

Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we're setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

 

Control Management maintains a strong and consistent control environment through a joint accountability model that aligns managers with each function and region to mitigate operational risk. The team focuses on four areas: Control Design & Expertise, Risks & Controls Identification/Assessment, Issues & Control Deficiencies and Control Governance & Reporting.

My services have been retained to recruit a **Plant Manager** for one of the top mid-sized U.S. dairy manufacturing companies. Opportunity located in desirable Midwest **metropolitan community**.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Market Director of Operations**

**Coverage Area: Kansas (KC, Laurence, Overland Park) and Iowa (Davenport and Des Moines)**

**Job Summary**

The Market Director is a key operational leader responsible for the performance of a geographic network of BHG treatment centers. This role directly leads and develops Program Directors and, through those leaders, is accountable for the operational, clinical, financial, and team performance of each treatment center within the market.

This is an opportunity for an experienced multi-site healthcare leader who enjoys developing people, improving performance, solving complex operational challenges, and expanding access to high-quality patient care.

The Market Director is accountable for building a high-performing market that delivers exceptional patient care, operational excellence, strong leadership, and sustainable growth. The Market Director will also perform duties within the scope of their license or certification when applicable, as outlined in an addendum to this job description.

**What You’ll Be Accountable For**

As Market Director, you will:

* Build high-performing leaders and create a culture of accountability.
* Deliver strong operational execution and financial performance.
* Ensure outstanding patient outcomes and timely access to care.
* Maintain regulatory excellence and operational integrity.
* Drive sustainable growth through referrals and community engagement.

**Key Areas of Responsibility**

**Leadership Development**

* Mentor, coach, and develop high-performing Program Directors and other market leaders.
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Build an engaged, patient-centered culture across treatment centers.
* Strengthen team member retention and develop succession plans for key leadership roles.
* Identify and develop future leaders within the organization.

**Clinical Excellence**

Partner with the Group Vice President and clinical leadership to improve and optimize key areas of clinical performance, including:

* True Counseling.
* Time to First Dose.
* Dose Stabilization.
* Patient Retention.
* Regulatory readiness.
* Patient outcomes.

**Operational Excellence**

* Ensure consistent execution of the BHG operating model across treatment centers.
* Optimize patient access, admissions, and census growth.
* Improve operational efficiency and labor productivity.
* Identify and remove barriers impacting treatment center performance.
* Establish and reinforce best practices across the market.
* Use performance data to identify opportunities and drive meaningful improvement.

**Patient Care & Clinical Excellence**

* Improve patient outcomes and the overall patient experience.
* Increase patient satisfaction.
* Ensure timely access to treatment.
* Support clinical quality initiatives.
* Promote a culture where patient-centered care remains at the heart of operational decisions.

**Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management**

* Maintain a strong culture of regulatory compliance and operational integrity.
* Ensure treatment centers are prepared for DEA, accreditation, and other regulatory inspections.
* Reinforce adherence to policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
* Identify and minimize operational and compliance risks.
* Partner closely with Clinical and Regulatory leadership.

**Workforce Excellence**

Partner with Talent, Performance & Workforce Strategy to ensure:

* Appropriate staffing levels across the market.
* Effective onboarding of new team members and leaders.
* Ongoing leadership development.
* Strong employee engagement.
* Improved retention and workforce stability.

**How You’ll Lead**

Successful Market Directors at BHG:

* Lead with integrity and sound judgment.
* Maintain a strong, visible presence in the field.
* Develop people and build strong leadership teams.
* Make timely, thoughtful decisions.
* Set clear expectations and hold teams accountable.
* Build trust across all levels of the organization.
* Identify and remove barriers to success.
* Balance strategy with disciplined execution.
* Never compromise patient care.

**What Success Looks Like**

Within your first year, you will have:

* Built a high-performing team of Program Directors.
* Increased patient access through stronger admissions and census growth.
* Improved clinical quality and patient outcomes.
* Strengthened employee engagement and retention.
* Improved operational and financial performance.
* Established a culture of accountability and consistent execution.
* Identified and developed future leaders.
* Helped position BHG as the nation’s leading provider of outpatient opioid treatment.

**What You’ll Bring**

* Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
* Demonstrated success leading multi-site healthcare operations through transformational change and organizational growth.
* Experience managing treatment or healthcare services across economically and culturally diverse communities.
* Strong understanding of healthcare industry dynamics.
* An operational and clinical excellence mindset, with the ability to adapt to changing market conditions.
* Proven ability to inspire, develop, and lead high-performing teams.
* Ability to think strategically about growth while remaining highly engaged in day-to-day operational execution.
* Strong financial and P&L acumen.
* Ability to establish and maintain positive relationships within treatment centers and across the broader organization and community.
* High integrity and sound judgment.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

**Disclaimer**

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by team members assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Team members may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed, and this job description may be updated at any time.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Who we are 
 With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. 
 
 What we need 
 Symbotic is seeking a Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing to join our Strategic Sourcing team within our Supply Chain organization. Your role will be to lead our contract manufacturing strategy and develop a resilient, cost-competitive global manufacturing network for complex electromechanical products.

 What we do 
 Our global procurement organization partners closely with the business to build category strategies that drive competitive advantage. We own strategic sourcing and supplier agreements end-to-end — from commercial and pricing structures through supplier relationship management — while our sourcing operations ensure disciplined execution at scale. Our scope spans the full lifecycle: procuring robotics, structural, and automation components at the core of our systems, sourcing third-party partners for installation and deployment, and ensuring robust aftersales support once systems are live — all in service of Symbotic's commitment to reimagining the supply chain and transforming the movement of goods through intelligent automation, while bringing unparalleled value to the customer. Every decision is grounded in a relentless focus on total cost of ownership, balancing speed and rigor to drive the best outcomes for the business.

 What you'll do 
 Lead Symbotic's contract manufacturing strategy, including selection, negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing management of global manufacturing partners.
 Own commercial relationships with key contract manufacturers and assembly suppliers, driving cost, quality, delivery, and capacity performance.
 Develop and execute sourcing strategies for complex electromechanical products, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing teams.
 Negotiate long-term supply agreements, manufacturing service agreements (MSAs), pricing, tooling, inventory, and capacity commitments.
 Drive annual cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, should-cost analysis, productivity programs, and supply base optimization.
 Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp activities to ensure suppliers meet schedule, quality, and cost objectives.
 Lead executive-level supplier business reviews and establish performance management scorecards and corrective action processes.
 Assess and mitigate supply chain risks related to capacity, geographic concentration, financial stability, and component availability.
 Partner with commodity sourcing teams across mechanical, electronics, motors, batteries, and other key categories to optimize total system cost.
 Develop manufacturing footprint strategies to support business growth, scalability, resiliency, and customer requirements.
 Manage significant annual spend and contribute to long-range supply chain, inventory, and working capital strategies.
 Build and mentor a high-performing sourcing organization as the business scales. 
 
 What you'll need 
 Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management , Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree or MBA is highly preferred.   
 Minimum 8–10 years of strategic sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, or procurement experience in robotics, automation, industrial equipment, electronics, or other complex hardware industries.
 Minimum 3 years of people management experience leading and growing teams.
 Deep experience managing contract manufacturers or similar EMS/mechanical assembly providers.
 Proven track record negotiating complex commercial agreements and delivering measurable cost reductions.
 Experience supporting product launches, manufacturing transfers, and global production ramp-ups.
 Strong understanding of electromechanical systems, including mechanical assemblies, motors, electronics, batteries, and custom manufactured components.
 Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and effectively communicate with executive leadership and strategic suppliers.
 Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams and driving results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. 
 
 Our Environment 
 Up to 20% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ.
 Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc.

**Plant Manager**

Manchester, CT United States | req34380

**What you will enjoy doing\***

* Lead and inspire plant operations, overseeing production, maintenance, quality, safety, and financial performance to deliver exceptional results
* Drive operational excellence by developing and executing strategies that achieve production goals, reduce waste, enhance quality, and maximize efficiency
* Promote a world-class safety culture, ensuring compliance with all regulatory, environment and workplace safety standards while protecting employees and operations.
* Build and develop high-performing teams by fostering a culture of engagement, accountability, innovation, and continuous learning
* Serve as a strategic leader, balancing day-to operational execution with long-term planning to support sustainable growth and operational excellence

**What makes you great**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline required.
* 7+ years of manufacturing leadership experience with a demonstrated history of delivering operational results, achieving production goals, and leading continuous improvement initiatives
* Exceptional leadership and communication skills with the ability to inspire, develop, and engage teams while building strong relationships across all levels of the organization
* Comprehensive understanding of manufacturing processes, equipment, and quality systems, coupled with a commitment to operational excellence
* Knowledge of safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements with a track record of maintaining compliance and promoting culture of workplace safety
* Results-oriented mindset with the ability to balance strategic thinking and hands-on leadership in a fast-paced manufacturing environment

**Why you will love working with us**

Linde is a leading global industrial gases and engineering company with 2025 sales of $34 billion. We live our mission of making our world more productive every day by providing high-quality solutions, technologies and services which are making our customers more successful and helping to sustain, decarbonize and protect our planet.
 
 
Linde serves a variety of end markets such as chemicals & energy, food & beverage, electronics, healthcare, manufacturing, metals and mining. Linde’s industrial gases and technologies are used in countless applications, enabling space exploration and launch technologies, delivering ultra-high-purity and specialty gases for semiconductor manufacturing, providing life-saving medical oxygen and enabling clean hydrogen production and carbon capture to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Linde also delivers state-of-the-art gas processing solutions to support customer growth, efficiency improvements and emissions reductions.

**What we offer you!**

At Linde, the sky is not the limit. If you’re looking to build a career where your work reaches beyond your job description and betters the people with whom you work, the communities we serve, and the world in which we all live, at Linde, your opportunities are limitless. Be Linde. Be Limitless. 
 
Linde offers competitive compensation and an outstanding benefits package. Enjoy access to health, dental, disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and vacation, 401(k) matching, pension benefits, an employee discount program, and opportunities for educational and professional growth. Additional compensation may vary depending on the position and organizational level. Build your future with us while making an impact every day! The pay range for this position is: $133,840 - $184,030

**Have we inspired you? Let´s talk about it**

We are looking forward to receiving your complete application.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other reason prohibited by applicable law. 
 
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc. abides by applicable export control laws including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) in accordance with the company's export control procedures. As such, persons considered for this position must be either a U.S. Citizen, Permanent Resident (green card holder) or otherwise classifiable as a U.S. person under relevant regulations. 
 
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc. acts responsibly towards its shareholders, business partners, employees, society and the environment in every one of its business areas, regions and locations across the globe. The company is committed to technologies and products that unite the goals of customer value and sustainable development. 
 

* The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position. Therefore employees assigned may be required to perform additional job tasks required by the manager.

R10104634 Plant Manager (Open)

Location:

Chester, VA - ASU

**How will you CONTRIBUTE and GROW?**
-------------------------------------

The primary function of this job is to operate large Airgas facilities safely and reliably by complying with regulatory requirements, developing and leading personnel, managing costs effectively, and developing personal skills and competencies. “Large” facilities generally are complex facilities that generally include multiple plants or technologies, supply criticality, 8 or more direct reports or multiple locations.

**Airgas is hiring for a Plant Manager in Chester, VA!**

 

***We are looking for you!***

 

* Work Schedule - Monday - Friday
* Comprehensive Family Benefits: Airgas offers a full benefits package designed to support your whole life, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance.
* Support for Parents: We offer a 14-week paid child birth benefit to support growing families.
* Future Security: 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, Tuition Assistance, Paid Holidays, Vacation, and Sick time.
Early Access: Your benefits start after just 30 days of employment 

 

**Recruiter:** Jacob ( Jacob.braithwaite@airliquide.com ) Phone: 980-445-9764 Call or Text 
 
 
 
**The primary function of this job is to operate large Airgas facilities safely and reliably by complying with regulatory requirements, developing and leading personnel, managing costs effectively, and developing personal skills and competencies. “Large” facilities generally are complex facilities that generally include multiple plants or technologies, supply criticality, 8 or more direct reports or multiple location** s. 
 
 
 
**Operational Duties:**

* This role encompasses a wide range of responsibilities, including fully supporting, accurately completing, and maintaining all company Health, Safety, and Environmental policies, procedures, and documentation as required.
* The Plant Manager III is ultimately accountable and responsible for site safety including employees, contractors, visitors and neighbors. Other essential tasks include meeting or exceeding company safety standards, demonstrating strong safety leadership and commitment and implementing and maintaining the training matrix and Airgas University training for the site.
* The individual in this role will own Key Operating Documents, maintain updated red-lines at all times, and display a detailed understanding of content and significance of each document. In addition to this, the job requires making plant and process decisions, performing process troubleshooting, establishing clear delegation of this authority to trained subordinates, fostering positive customer and intercompany department relationships, delivering the quality and quantity of product required by the business and executing predictive and preventive maintenance to eliminate catastrophic failures and unplanned maintenance.
Furthermore, the role includes developing annual maintenance plans and turn-around planning as needed and sets and maintains high housekeeping standards to exemplify and improve the company image. 

 

**Regulatory Requirements:**

* The individual in this role is expected to operate the facility in compliance with all local and federal governmental regulations Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Department of Transportation (DOT), Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP), etc) and company policies. This role also includes maintaining and complying with all necessary licenses and permits, providing all regulatory training and maintaining documentation, reporting and investigating all incidents and ensuring corrective actions are complete.
Other key duties include k eeping plant hazard analysis current and displaying thorough knowledge of possible hazards and associated safeguards as well as adhering to Management of Change procedure. This role also ensures that all performance evaluations, hiring, promotions and assignments are free of any form of discrimination; Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). 

 

**Safety & Compliance Functions:**

This role includes a commitment to strict adherence to company policies, safety guidelines, and procedural standards, as well as a focus on modeling exemplary safety behavior, leading by personal example, working to achieve “Zero Accidents” by taking a leadership role in safety, implementing and ensuring compliance to the Qualification and Training program for Production Technicians. 

 

**Communication & Collaboration:**

This role is expected to conduct an annual performance review with each employee, implement individual development plans annually and provide training and coaching to improve performance, provide candid constructive input to management decisions and actively support those decisions as well as adhering to administrative and operational policies and procedures. 

 

**Financial Management:**

* This role requires the understanding, monitoring and optimizing of operating costs within an authorized budget and the ability to identify and implement opportunities to reduce costs within delegated authorization.
* Additionally, the position involves participation in the Capital Planning Process and the Yearly Expense Budgeting Process . In addition to this, the job requires the c ontrol of overtime within established limits and c ontinuously improving efficiency and availability indicators and utilizing national purchasing agreements and frame agreements.

**\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
----------------------------------------------------

**Are you a MATCH?**
--------------------

**To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each job duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.**

 

**Required Education:**

Mechanical or Chemical Engineering degree preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience acceptable 

 

**Required Length & Type of Experience:**

* 8+ years process industry experience.
Mechanical or Chemical Engineering degree is an advantage. 

 

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:**

 

* Technical and working understanding of the Air Separation or Carbon Dioxide liquefaction plant process or applicable process plant industry experience.
* Familiarity with regulatory requirements for operating plants, including Process Safety Management, OSHA regulations, EPA regulations, EEOC guidelines, FDA regulations (where applicable), state and local requirements.
* Strong computer and business application skills.
* Trainable on Distributed Process Control (DCS) or Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) operation and troubleshooting.
* Able to deliver and explain training material to operating personnel.
* Extremely organized and effective at time management – able to establish and maintain a plant filing system and control of engineering documents. Ability to read and red-line key operating documents.
* Displays mechanical and electrical aptitude for equipment operation and troubleshooting.
* Working knowledge of commercial agreements and Air Liquide customer relations.
* Excellent communication and team leadership skills.
High understanding of accounting principles and working knowledge of plant operating budget. 

 

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

**The characteristics listed below are representative of the physical demands required by an individual to successfully perform the essential duties of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.**

 

* Ability to work extended hours as business needs dictate.
* On call nights, weekends and holidays as required.
* Occasional travel required – typically 1 to 6 trips per year.
Willing to relocate for a promotional opportunity. 

 

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

**The characteristics listed below are representative of the work environment typically encountered by an individual while performing the essential duties of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.**

 

* Frequent regional travel.
* Moderate overnight travel.
* Must have reliable, appropriate transportation.
Job requires visitation to various Airgas and customer sites, which have varying environments/conditions, layouts, and accessibility. 

 
 

**NOTE:** The above stated duties are intended to outline those functions typically performed by individuals assigned to this classification. This description of duties is not intended to be all-inclusive or to limit the discretionary authority of supervisors to assign other tasks of similar nature or level of responsibility nor does it imply an employment agreement nor does it imply an employment agreement.

 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Benefits**

We care about and support our Airgas Families. This is evident not only through our competitive compensation but also through a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision plans, short-term and long-term disability, life and accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), pre-tax commuter transportation benefit, parental leave, vacation, sick time, floating holidays, jury duty and funeral/bereavement leave, and paid holidays for all eligible full-time employees.

Additionally, we offer our eligible employees a 401k plan with company matching funds, tuition reimbursement, discounted college tuition for eligible employees’ dependents, and an Airgas Scholarship Program for dependent children.

Associates who are members of collective bargaining units should review their bargaining agreement to determine whether they are eligible for some or all of the benefits described here and to see any special terms or conditions for eligibility.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Your DIFFERENCES enhance our PERFORMANCE**

At Airgas, we are committed to building a workplace that embraces the diversity of our employees, our customers, patients, community stakeholders and cultures across the world.

We welcome and consider applications from all qualified applicants, regardless of their race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, disability or any other protected characteristic. We strongly believe a diverse organization opens up opportunities for people to express their talent, both individually and collectively and it helps foster our ability to innovate by living our fundamentals, acting for our success and creating an engaging environment in a changing world.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**About Airgas**

Airgas, an Air Liquide company, is a leading U.S. supplier of industrial, medical and specialty gases, as well as hardgoods and related products; one of the largest U.S. suppliers of safety products; and a leading U.S. supplier of ammonia products and process chemicals. Through the passion and diversity of its 18,000 associates, Airgas fosters a culture of safety, customer success, sustainability and innovation.
