Our five Core Values empower us to achieve Our Purpose:

**Patient Focus, Integrity, Innovation, Impact and Empathy.**

 

Learn more about Life at Olympus: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers.

**Job Description**
-------------------

This position provides quality operations leadership to the global distribution operation. The Director of Quality role will provide Quality leadership for the Global Ship Hold process. This scope will include ownership, monitoring and communication of the Global Ship Hold process. In addition, this role will be responsible for managing global strategy and implementation for the quality requirements for inventory handling, segregation and reporting. This position partners closely with the Global Supply Chain Management.

**Job Duties**
--------------

* Serves as the global process owner (GPO) for the Global Ship Hold Process.
* Monitors and manages the initiation, progress and release of global ship holds.
* Develops and executes global communication on the status and action plan of existing global ship holds.
* Partners with the Field Corrective Action (FCA) team on inventory handling and reconciliation of open projects.
* Develops strategic priorities for the global control, disposition and resolution of quality processes for material control.
* Works with regional management and staff to ensure the successful execution of established policies and procedures for inventory management.
* Serves as a global leader to focus a matrixed network of Ship Hold Coordinators.
* Continued monitoring of staff performance to ensure quality and consistency.
* Performs all other duties as directed.

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

**Required:**

* BA/BS degree or equivalent in a Life Science, Engineering, or Supply Chain management. Advanced technical degree and/or MBA preferred.
* A minimum of 10 years of cGMP experience in quality management or operations within the MedTech industry.
* Experience with durable medical devices, and a strong understanding of supply chain processes and inventory controls (reverse logistics is a plus).
* Demonstrated experience influencing senior level management, key stakeholders and leveraging crossfunctional partnerships for successful execution of critical quality initiatives.
* Experience interpreting and applying business requirements and regulations (FDA and other applicable global authorities) into sustainable quality processes leveraging industry best practices.
* Experience with global inventory processes and systems (ERP) – including hold mechanisms.
* Experience with warehouse management processes and systems (WMS) including product segregation and control on non-conforming material.
* Proactive approach to quality and compliance, with a focus on innovation and adaptation in a fast -paced environment. Strong ability to think and act globally, be fearless change agent while managing risks, develop future visions and engage audiences to drive transformation.
* Capable of presenting clear and insightful thoughts based in facts and data gain trust, build confidence and to influence key stakeholders across the business.
* Persistence to continuously improve, never settling for status quo, while keeping customer satisfaction and customer value central.
* Must be a self -starter with high personal accountability and courage to always do the right thing.
* Driving cultural change in a complex and diverse Olympus organization.
* Will work with global teams, availability will include working across global time zones. Travel up to 25% possible.

**Why join

Reporting to the President, C.E.O., Directs and coordinates activities of personnel at all Hutchinson Sealing Systems facilities engaged in Quality Management System to prevent or eliminate defects in new or existing products or process by performing the following duties personally or through subordinates. * Participates with other top management personnel in formulating and establishing company policies, operating procedures, and goals.
* Participates in review of product development activities and APQP milestones.
* Conducts Quality System Management review meetings with top management to assess performance and compliance to customer quality requirements.
* Reviews technical problems and procedures of departments and recommends solutions to problems or changes in procedures.
* Confers with engineers and managers about quality assurance of new products and process to improve manufacturing capability.
* Reviews technical publications, articles, and abstracts to stay abreast of technical and quality system developments in industry.
* Travel required on a frequent basis to suppliers and customer facilities as well as other Hutchinson facilities.

Master's degree (M.A.) or equivalent; or four to ten years’ related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Qualifications may be waived by management. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

None.

Manages subordinates in department. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. record.ROLE_TEXT:
What if... we could build the operational backbone that gets Flagship's most transformative medicines from the lab bench to the patient, reliably and at scale?

Pioneering Medicines (PM), an initiative of Flagship Pioneering, is building a world-class biopharmaceutical R&D capability focused on conceiving and developing life-changing treatments for patients by harnessing the power of Flagship's scientific platforms and applying those innovative approaches to serious diseases with unmet medical need. Unique to Pioneering Medicines' approach is the opportunity to combine platforms to create truly novel and potentially transformative treatments.

**About Flagship Pioneering:**

Flagship Pioneering conceives, creates, resources, and develops first-in-category life science platform companies to transform human health and sustainability. Since its founding in 2000, the firm has originated and fostered the development of more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in over $34 billion in aggregate value, 500+ issued patents, and more than 50 clinical trials for novel therapeutic agents.

**Position Summary:**

We are seeking a Senior Director, Supply Operations with a proven track record of establishing and running supply chain and operations functions within a fast-paced pharmaceutical or biotech environment, including supporting multiple emerging-modality programs simultaneously. This leader will build and lead the Supply Operations function within Technical Operations (TechOps), owning supply chain management and shaping the operating model that connects technical teams with external partners, and jointly leading vendor management responsibilities. This position reports to the VP, Strategy & Operations, TechOps.

This leader will own the strategy and design of how material and product flow from external partners through to animal / clinical studies, lead day-to-day coordination in partnership with technical SMEs, and serve as an operational point of contact for Pioneering Medicines' CDMOs and suppliers. This role operates at the intersection of science, strategy, and operations, setting supply direction across a complex multimodality pipeline and building external supply operations as a competitive advantage for Pioneering Medicines. As a build-and-own mandate, this role will define and scale a lean, phase-appropriate operating model (the systems and processes) that accommodates the distinct supply requirements of multiple and emerging modalities and grows with the organization and strategic direction.

**Responsibilities:**

* Lead and design the Supply Operations function within TechOps, directing supply chain management and jointly leading vendor management responsibilities. Own strategy, roadmap, and investment decisions for the function, and oversee budget and resourcing across an expanding portfolio of programs and modalities running simultaneously at different stages of development.

* Own end-to-end supply operations, including demand and supply planning, inventory management, cold chain/logistics, raw material sourcing coordination, lot and batch

management, and CDMO manufacturing scheduling, so material and product reach the clinic on schedule. Tailor supply models to the distinct needs of each modality (e.g., small molecules, biologics, nucleic acids/LNP, cell and gene therapies), including storage, shipping, shelf-life, and chain of identity/custody requirements.

* Serve as a senior operational point of contact for CDMOs and suppliers, leading day-to-day coordination (scheduling, shipments, issue resolution) jointly with the relevant technical SMEs. Build CDMO relationships and anticipate portfolio capacity needs for emerging modalities (e.g., viral vector, plasmid DNA, mRNA/LNP, cell therapy), balancing competing demand for CDMO slots, specialized raw materials, and resources across concurrent programs.

* Develop the function's core work instructions, SOPs, process flows, and supply chain network and capacity maps

**FLSA Status:** Exempt 
**Department:** Operations

**Summary**

The Director of Operations leads and optimizes Maury Microwave’s day-to-day manufacturing and operational activities at its Parsippany, New Jersey facility. This position provides leadership across key operational functions, including Material Planning and Control, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Assembly & Test, and Shipping.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide day-to-day leadership and direction for Maury Microwave’s Parsippany Operations organization, including Material Planning/Control, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Assembly & Test, and Shipping.
* Ensure effective execution of production plans and customer commitments while maintaining appropriate standards for quality, cost, safety, and delivery.
* Drive improvements in On-Time Delivery (OTD) through disciplined production planning, scheduling, material availability, capacity management, and cross-functional coordination.
* Proactively identify production constraints, material shortages, capacity issues, quality concerns, and other risks that may affect customer delivery.
* Establish, monitor, and drive meaningful operational KPIs, including On-Time Delivery, productivity, efficiency, quality, inventory, labor utilization, capacity, and other appropriate operational measures.
* Establish a consistent operating cadence for reviewing performance, identifying gaps, assigning corrective actions, and ensuring accountability for results.
* Provide regular operational performance reports and updates to the VP Technical Operations and other members of the Senior Leadership Team
* Utilize Lean manufacturing principles and structured problem-solving methodologies to improve quality, productivity, efficiency, cost, and timeliness.
* Improve production planning, scheduling, workflow, capacity management, and shop-floor visibility.
* Partner with Quality to ensure manufacturing processes consistently meet customer, regulatory, and company quality requirements.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Management, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. Master’s degree preferred.

* Demonstrated success improving On-Time Delivery, productivity, quality, operational efficiency, and manufacturing performance.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, scheduling, supply chain, inventory management, Lean principles, and continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated ability to establish and manage operational KPIs and drive accountability for measurable results.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Strong analytical, organizational, decision-making, and problem-solving capabilities.
* Ability to operate effectively in a hands-on, fast-paced, technically complex manufacturing environment.

Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. **Job Summary:** Responsible for constructing cabinets and their components through assembly and sub-assembly of various components and materials.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Assemble various cabinet components and materials.
* Safely operate assigned equipment.
* Proficiently use a tape measure to determine sizes for parts.
* Maintain no more than a one-percent rejection rate per workday.
* Supply the sufficient amount of parts in the buffers established by the schedule.
* Inspect component parts prior to working on them and again after they have been machined for correct specifications.

**Qualifications:**

* Must have a high school diploma or equivalent.
* Must have mathematical skills to take measurements on cabinets and materials.
* Must have corrected hearing to listen to needs and instructions of managers and coworkers, and listen to the environment to be aware of surroundings.
* Must have corrected vision to be aware of surroundings and locations of items needed.
* Should have knowledge of/or ability to use a tape measure, saws, drills, and other hand tools.
* Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment.

**Essential Functions of the Job:**

* Stands and walks up to a total of ten hours per day on a concrete surface.
* Lifts and carries cabinets, parts, and tools in accordance with the requirements listed in the matrices below, frequently and repetitively for up to ten hours a day.
* Pushes and pulls items in accordance with the requirements listed in the matrices below in order to transfer components for assembly.
* Bends and stoops to reach areas difficult to access.
* Performs twisting and rotation motions using head/neck, waist, knees, and arms while assembling cabinets.
* Frequently reaches in order to attach parts and complete final assembly of cabinets.
* Handles drills, hand tools, hardware, and cabinet parts. Handling may be done unilaterally (one-handed) or bilaterally (two-handed) depending on the size and shape of the task being performed.
* Constantly uses fingers in order to attach hardware, doors, and various parts to finished cabinets.
* Must be mentally alert and capable of remembering faces, names, oral instructions, and details of varying types and sizes of materials and cabinets.
* Must be able to communicate effectively with management and coworkers by phone or in-person.
* Must be mentally altered and capable of remembering oral instructions and routine tasks.
* Must be able to withstand fluctuations in temperature and environmental fluctuations.
* Must be able to work the required daily and weekly work hours as determined by the schedule.
* Good attendance and punctuality are necessary.
* Must exemplify through appearance and behavior the company’s image of excellence.
* Must be alert and able to identify and respond to a hazard by either reporting it immediately, or by taking corrective measures if directed.

The ideal candidate is a proven cement manufacturing leader with extensive experience managing plant operations, including production, maintenance and reliability, quality, engineering, process optimization, safety, environmental compliance, and capital projects. This individual will combine strong technical knowledge of cement manufacturing with business and financial acumen, including experience managing operating and capital budgets, improving equipment reliability and plant efficiency, and controlling manufacturing costs. We are looking for a visible, hands-on leader who develops strong teams, drives accountability, and has a demonstrated ability to improve safety, reliability, quality, production, and overall plant performance.
 
 
**Who we are:** 
GCC is a world-class company that produces, distributes and markets cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, and innovative products related to the construction industries in Mexico and the United States. We take pride in being a market leader with a culture of innovation, high performance and safety. GCC offers a very competitive benefits program including paid time off, medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability insurance plans, and a 401K.
 
 
**What you will do:** 
Directs, coordinates and administers all production, quality control, maintenance, engineering, purchasing and process control activities required in meeting the operations budget objectives and maintains alignment with the strategic plans of GCCA for the preservation of the plant's physical assets and to meet projected sales goals. Directs and coordinates activities to obtain optimum efficiency and economy of operations and maximize profits by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate managers and supervisors.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations is responsible for supporting and executing enterprise operational oversight across multiple behavioral health service lines and locations. This role partners closely with the VP of Operations and executive leadership to ensure operational stability, scalability, compliance, staffing coordination, workflow management, and organizational performance across all assigned programs.

The Director of Operations serves as a key operational leader responsible for driving consistency, accountability, and operational execution across outpatient behavioral health programs, recovery support services, housing operations, nursing home partnerships, and future organizational growth initiatives.

This is a non-clinical leadership role. The Director of Operations does not provide clinical supervision or determine clinical level of care decisions, but works collaboratively with Clinical, Revenue Cycle, Housing, Intake, Human Resources, and Executive Leadership teams to ensure efficient and compliant operational performance across the enterprise.

This position requires the ability to exercise sound independent judgment, make operational decisions autonomously when appropriate, prioritize competing organizational needs, and respond effectively to rapidly changing operational demands across multiple service lines and locations.

This position is designed to support long-term operational leadership continuity across the organization. Responsibilities may expand or shift based on organizational structure, operational needs, leadership transitions, and enterprise growth initiatives.

**Essential Responsibilities**

* Enterprise Operational Oversight

* Assist with operational oversight of outpatient behavioral health clinics, recovery support services, housing operations, nursing home partnerships, and future service expansions
* Ensure operational consistency, accountability, and workflow execution across enterprise locations
* Monitor operational performance, staffing needs, workflow barriers, and service delivery coordination
* Independently identify operational issues and implement timely solutions within the scope of organizational expectations
* Exercise independent decision-making related to operational workflow management, staffing coordination, scheduling adjustments, and day-to-day operational needs
* Assist with development and implementation of operational systems, policies, workflows, and accountability structures
* Identify operational inefficiencies and implement process improvement initiatives
* Support organizational scalability and stabilization efforts

**Staffing & Workflow Management**

* Oversee operational scheduling processes and staffing coordination across assigned programs
* Monitor staffing coverage, workflow efficiency, transportation coordination, and operational throughput
* Collaborate with department leaders regarding staffing support, scheduling concerns, and operational barriers
* Make operational decisions related to staffing coverage, workflow prioritization, and operational resource allocation when appropriate
* Ensure operational follow-up on workflow disruptions, scheduling gaps, cancellations, and staffing needs
* Support census oversight, operational capacity management, and throughput planning

**Interdepartmental Leadership**

* Partner collaboratively with Clinical, Housing, Revenue Cycle, Intake, Human Resources, Compliance, and Executive Leadership teams
* Support organizational alignment between operational and clinical departments
* Participate in leadership meetings, operational huddles, and enterprise plannin

The Opportunity
 
 
The St. Jude Leadership Academy is building the systems, experiences and capabilities that help leaders across St. Jude grow their impact. We’re looking for a Director of Academy Operations who can help turn that vision into an enterprise-scale reality.

This is a role for a builder.

 
 

As the Academy’s primary operational leader and integrator, you’ll translate strategy into an integrated portfolio of work and create the infrastructure needed to move ideas from concept through implementation, evaluation and scale. You’ll work across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and institutional partners to connect priorities, clarify ownership and turn complex, cross-functional work into coordinated action.

You’ll also serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, bringing visibility to priorities, tradeoffs, resources and execution risks while helping shape how the Academy delivers its work across St. Jude.

Because the Leadership Academy operates as a small, highly collaborative team, this isn’t a role where strategy gets handed off once the plan is built. You’ll move comfortably between enterprise-level thinking and hands-on execution, building the systems that allow a small team to have an outsized impact across St. Jude.

 
 

### **What You’ll Do**

As Director of Academy Operations, you will:

* **Turn strategy into execution.** Translate Leadership Academy priorities into an integrated portfolio, implementation roadmap and operating plan.
* **Lead complex work from idea to impact.** Guide cross-functional initiatives from concept and design through implementation, evaluation and scale.
* **Build the Academy’s operating infrastructure.** Establish governance, decision points, roles, handoffs, planning processes and operating rhythms that create clarity and accountability.
* **Connect work across St. Jude.** Build strong partnerships across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and other institutional functions, bringing people and priorities together while maintaining clear roles and ownership.
* **See around corners.** Identify dependencies, duplication, capacity constraints, gaps and execution risks across the Academy’s portfolio and drive solutions.
* **Create visibility into impact.** Establish portfolio-level measures, dashboards and reporting that show progress, outcomes and organizational impact.
* **Help good ideas scale.** Develop practical approaches for moving promising concepts and pilots into sustainable institutional practices.
* **Lead operational and resource planning.** Oversee budgets, resources, technology, vendors, contracts and external partnerships that support the Academy’s work.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Apply human-centered design, agile and continuous-improvement approaches to strengthen programs, processes and operations.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor.** Help senior leadership navigate priorities, tradeoffs, sequencing, resource allocation and execution risk.
* **Communicate with influence.** Develop executive-level materials and clearly communicate progress, decisions, risks and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
* **Stay close to the work.** Remain directly involved in execution when needed, reflecting the hands-on, highly collaborative nature of the Academy team.
* **Develop people and teams.** Create clarity around goals and expectations while supporting performance, engagement, professional growth and meaningful career experiences.

Job area: Managerial

**DSV - Global transport and logistics**
 
In 1976, ten independent haulers joined forces and founded DSV in Denmark. Since then, DSV has evolved to become the world's 3rd largest supplier of global solutions within transport and logistics. Today, we add value to our customers' entire supply chain by transporting, storing, packaging, re-packaging, processing and clearing all types of goods. We work every day from our many offices in more than 80 countries to ensure a steady supply of goods to production lines, outlets, stores and consumers all over the world. Our reach is global, yet our presence is local and close to our customers. Read more at www.dsv.com

 

**Location**: USA - Fort Worth, 9401 Hemphill St

**Division**: Solutions

**Job Posting Title**: Director, Operations

**Time Type**: Full Time

 

**SUMMARY**

The Director of Operations provides overall direction and guidance to the operational activities of the organization. Provides strategic leadership and management to Operations within a large geographic region. The Regional Director of Operations will strive to maximize growth and profitability while responsibly managing the resources of their region according to the company and client expectations and policies. Develops and implements long and short-term strategies to achieve financial and growth targets. Develops emerging talent and successors and creates a work environment that promotes the values of DSV.

 

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Responsible for supporting the company strategy including growth and transformational initiatives.
* Develop regional strategies to align with enterprise targets.
* Ensure targets are achieved and local needs are also met.
* Plans and budgets regional financial targets.
* Responsible for ensuring results are achieved against targets.
* Ensure operational excellence within and across our core services.
* Ensures operational excellence through standardization of existing practices, risk assessment and review of key metrics.
* Provides leadership and creates an environment that fosters passion, teamwork and agility within the organization.
* Ensures initiatives are developed and executed in the selection and development of talent and creates an environment that improves associate engagement.
* Build and sustains long-term client relationships.
* Supports local, regional and global sales initiatives by partnering with key clients and delivering a high level of client focus to business initiatives.
* Plans and successfully execute start-up facilities for new business.
* Spearheads teams and partners with clients to trouble-shoot and solve existing issues or problems.
* Contributes as a key member to our sales and solutions team in winning key strategic accounts.
* Develops and implements an operations strategy tailored to our client that identifies opportunities to improve cost control and margin improvement and will lead to organic growth.
* Consistently works within a complex matrixed environment.
* Works collaboratively and establishes solid business relationships with supporting departments including but not limited to: Human Resources, Sales, and Finance.
 

**OTHER DUTIES**

* Performs special projects as required
 

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* The Regional Director of Operations directly supervises General Managers.
* Responsible for overall management to achieve client satisfaction.
* Must interpret policies, purposes, and goals of the organization for subordinates.
* Responsible for performance management of direct reports.
* Builds bench strength by leading, developing and challenging operations teams to raise individual and collective performance levels by demonstrating and promoting discretionary effort.

Join EBAD and you'll be a part of a team who creates cutting edge technology that will blast us into the future. No other company can match the innovative energetic solutions that we provide. **Shape the Future. Deliver Excellence. Achieve Zero Failure.**
At
**Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense (EBAD),**
we’ve been innovating for nearly
**200 years,**
delivering mission-critical technologies that protect lives and advance exploration. As we prepare to double in size over the next 3–5 years, we’re investing in our people and culture to support this transformation.
 
 
We’re seeking a dynamic
**Director of Quality**
to lead a complex, multi-site quality organization and drive performance at scale. Based at our headquarters in Simsbury, Connecticut, this role is critical to ensure the highest levels of product integrity, compliance, and customer trust across a rapidly growing business. This is not just about maintaining standards but about building a future-state vision for quality that enables growth, safeguards mission success, and strengthens EBAD’s reputation as a trusted partner.
 
 
**The Opportunity:**
EBAD’s customers depend on us to deliver our products with zero failure in mission-critical environments. The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing and executing a strategic Quality Management System (QMS) while leading quality operations across multiple sites. This leader will be tasked with driving measurable quality improvement, while also championing a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
 
 
This is an exciting opportunity for a leader to make an immediate impact by providing direction, driving the strategy for the business, and developing a problem-solving culture.

* Quality & Compliance Leadership: Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries, with expertise in zero-failure mission environments.
* Continuous Improvement & Performance: Skilled in EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices with the ability to drive metrics-based improvement and systemic problem-solving.
* Team Development & Leadership: Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and build strong teams while fostering engagement and accountability.
* Collaboration & Influence: Strong cross-functional partnership with credibility to influence senior leadership, customers, and suppliers.
* Resilience & Adaptability: Able to manage ambiguity, drive change, and motivate teams in a fast-scaling environment.

**The Candidate We Are Looking For:**

* BS in an engineering discipline (MS preferred)
* Minimum 10 years of experience in high-mix, low-volume operations and manufacturing environment
* Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other mission-critical industries
* Demonstrated expertise in leading audits and managing compliance across regulatory bodies, customers, and suppliers, with deep knowledge of standards such as AS9100, ISO9001, and DoD requirements
* Proven ability to enhance customer quality by partnering closely with engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to consistently meet customer demand
* Strong record of measurable quality improvements
* Skilled in continuous improvement, performance metrics, and problem-solving through EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practic

Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.
 
 
Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.
 
 
As the
**Senior Manager of Quality System and Quality (Regulatory) Compliance**
, you are a pivotal leader responsible for the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of our Quality Management System (QMS), oversight, and associated tools. You will lead our efforts to ensure robust compliance with national and international medical device regulations, including FDA, ISO 13485, EU MDR, and MDSAP. This role is a unique blend of strategic foresight and tactical leadership, requiring a deep expertise in QMS setup and management, particularly for Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), with ability to make thoughtful changes and enhance the overall QMS.
 
 
You will lead a high-performing team of quality professionals , championing a "Quality-first" culture and driving data-driven decisions. Your proven track record of navigating complex regulatory landscapes, including
**FDA, PMDA, IEC, EU MDR, and ISO regulations and standards**
, is essential to our success.

Quality Management System (QMS) Oversight
 
 

* Manage holistic aspects of the QMS to ensure compliance with global regulations, including FDA, ISO 13485, EU MDR, and MDSAP countries’ requirements.
* Oversee the following key QMS subsystems: CAPA subsystem, Document Control, Training, Management Review, Internal Audits, and External Audit management, QMS Tool Validation, and Supplier Management.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the QMS.

Quality Compliance & Audits
 
 

* Serve as the front room or backroom lead and the primary subject matter expert (SME) for the QMS during audits, including inspections by the FDA, Notified Bodies, and other regulatory authorities.
* Prepare the organization for an appropriate level of quality compliance to U.S. and international requirements to support Heartflow’s global expansion.

Strategic Leadership & Team Development
 
 

* Lead, mentor, and scale a team of QMS professionals, fostering career growth and technical excellence.
* Champion a "Quality-first" mindset throughout the organization, through collaboration and using impactful KPIs to drive accountability and data-driven decisions.
* Collaborate with leaders and partners in R&D, Production, Regulatory, Clinical, and Product Management to integrate quality processes seamlessly, balancing compliance with business objectives.
* Manage departmental resources, including headcount and long-term strategic planning.

Skills Needed:

* Ability to coach, mentor, and drive a collaborative quality culture through influence.

The Plant Quality Assurance Senior Manager is responsible for developing and implementing quality policies and procedures to ensure production meets established standards. This role leads the quality function at the plant level, driving continuous improvement, regulatory compliance, and customer satisfaction.

### **Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead the development and execution of quality assurance protocols and testing models.
* Oversee sampling procedures, techniques, and equipment to ensure consistency and accuracy.
* Design and implement methods to maintain quality throughout the production lifecycle.
* Manage ongoing inspection, testing, analysis, and resolution processes to uphold quality standards.
* Identify quality variances and recommend corrective actions to maintain compliance with specifications.
* Ensure timely and cost-effective completion of quality-related projects.
* Lead and develop the Quality team, focusing on talent development, performance management, and succession planning.
* Collaborate with customers to define and resolve product quality issues and develop cost-effective quality programs.
* Review product designs and recommend specification revisions to enhance quality and manufacturability.
* Develop and execute quality management strategies aligned with short-term business goals and long-term objectives.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Six Sigma, SPC, and other statistical methodologies.
* Oversee calibration systems and repair depot operations for gauges, fixtures, instruments, and tooling.
* Maintain strong supplier relationships to ensure quality standards are met across the supply chain.
* Champion a culture of quality and employee engagement across all levels of the organization.

### **Qualifications:**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related industrial field required; Master’s degree preferred.
* Minimum of 8 years of relevant experience in manufacturing quality management, preferably in assembly processes.
* At least 3 years of direct management experience.
* Extensive knowledge of quality systems, policies, and procedures.
* Proven expertise in statistical analysis, SPC, DOE, root cause analysis, and data-driven problem solving.
* Demonstrated ability to present quality initiatives and solutions using ROI and business modeling.
* Strong written, verbal, presentation, and persuasion skills.
* Excellent organizational and computer skills.
* Effective leadership and people management capabilities.
* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to gain employee buy-in and foster collaboration.

**Other Work Requirements**

* This is an on-site role based in Orangeburg, SC (This position is 100% onsite)

Responsible for providing leadership and direction to Quality team(s) to ensure quality and compliance for the applicable products and processes for assigned department(s). Develop strategy, translate into functional plans and guide execution of long-term goals.

**Job Description**

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Direct the development of product specifications for Medline branded products; such as the testing requirements, procedures and methods for testing, inspecting or qualifying new products and suppliers.
* Partner with Supplier Audit department and Division to determine optimal Supplier relationship.
* Develop and implement strategy for the Quality department(s) based upon Quarterly Management Review.
* Prepare and deliver Customer presentations.
* Act as liaison with Senior Leadership of Divisions, Suppliers, Manufacturing, and/or Operations to ensure quality products, on time delivery, and customer satisfaction.
* Collaborate with Suppliers, manufacturing partners and product managers in developing and implementing QA programs.
* Oversee QSR for assigned department(s) and ensure compliance as measured by FDA/ISO/internal audits.
* Management responsibilities include:
* Typically, manages through multiple Managers. Provides leadership and management to one or more major departments of an operating unit or to a department that has system-wide accountability.
* Strategic, tactical and operational planning (12 + months) for the function or department;
* Direct budgetary responsibility for one or more departments, functions or major projects/programs;
* Interpret and execute policies for departments/projects and develops;
* Recommend and implement new policies or modifications to existing policies;
Hiring staff, recommending pay increases, performing performance reviews, training and development of staff, estimating personnel needs, assigning work, meeting completion dates, interpreting and ensuring consistent application of organizational policies. 

 

**MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:**

* Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, or Technical Field.

**Certification / Licensure:**

* None

**Work Experience:**

* At least 7 years of experience related to the design/operation of medical device or drug combination product platforms, design controls, risk management, including working in compliance with QSR/GMP/ISO requirements or other regulated industries (21CFR 820, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, MDSAP, and MDR).
* At least 4 years of management experience.

**Knowledge / Skills / Abilities:**

* Depth of technical knowledge of relevant standards and regulations (21CFR 820, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, MDSAP, and MDR etc.)
* Proficiency in analyzing and reporting data in order to identify issues, trends, or exceptions to drive improvement of results and find solutions.
* Demonstrated ability to control and coordinate concurrent projects, competing priorities and critical deadlines.
* Advanced level skill in Microsoft Excel (for example: using AVERAGE function, merging and centering cells, printing centered page and/or creating a pivot table).
Position requires travel up to 30% of the time for business purposes (within state, out of state and/or internationally).

**Education:**

* None

* None

**Work Experience:**

* At least 6 years of managerial experience preferred.
* At least 8 years of related experience in Medical Device, Pharmaceutical, Food, Cosmetic, or Personal Products industries preferred.

**Knowledge / Skills / Abilities:**

* None

**Job Title:** Regional Director of Operations 
**Reports To:** Director of Operations 
**FLSA Status:** Exempt 
**Job Type:** Full-Time with regular travel to assigned practice locations

**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Regional Director of Operations (RDO) provides high-level operational leadership and strategic oversight for a portfolio of at least 15 dental practices, representing significant aggregate EBITDA volume and diverse market conditions. The RDO directly manages Regional Managers and Office Managers, driving operational consistency, financial performance, and alignment with company objectives. This role is both strategic and hands-on, requiring advanced financial acumen, strong people leadership, and the ability to implement enterprise initiatives effectively across a large, complex region. The RDO acts as a primary field partner to the Director of Operations, contributing to strategic planning, operational innovation, and cross-functional collaboration to achieve growth and profitability targets. Must be located in South Florida, Texas or Missouri,

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Operational Leadership**

* Oversee day-to-day operations across a portfolio of at least 15 practices, ensuring adherence to IDS standards, policies, and performance expectations.
* Lead, coach, and develop Regional Managers and Office Managers to build strong, capable leadership teams within each location.
* Ensure consistent execution of operational workflows, patient experience standards, and compliance requirements.

### **Financial Performance**

* Monitor and drive key financial metrics, including revenue growth, EBITDA performance, expense management, and AR improvement.
* Partner with Finance to develop accurate forecasting and budgeting for assigned markets.
* Identify and act on opportunities to optimize profitability and operational efficiency across the portfolio.

### **People Leadership & Development**

* Provide regular performance coaching and career development for Regional Managers and Office Managers.
* Foster a positive and accountable culture, emphasizing continuous improvement and leadership excellence.
* Support succession planning and leadership readiness for key operational roles.

### **Strategic & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Partner with corporate departments (HR, Finance, RCM, Procurement, Clinical, Marketing, M&A) to implement enterprise initiatives at the regional level.
* Serve as a key point of escalation for complex operational, compliance, or personnel issues within the portfolio.
* Contribute to enterprise-level operational planning and strategic decision-making in partnership with the Director of Operations.

**Integration & Growth**

* Lead the integration of newly acquired practices within the assigned region, ensuring cultural alignment and operational readiness.
* Support market expansion efforts through operational due diligence, onboarding, and performance ramp-up.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Management, or related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 8–10 years of multi-site operational leadership experience, preferably in a dental service organization (DSO) or multi-unit healthcare environment.
* Proven track record of managing at least 15 locations or equivalent in aggregate business volume.
* Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and P&L management.
* Exceptional leadership, coaching, and team development skills.
* Strong problem-solving ability with a track record of improving operational performance.
* Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization.
* Willingness to travel regularly within assigned markets, up to 75%.

**Competencies**
----------------

* **Strategic Leadership** – Ability to translate enterprise goals into regional execution plans.

As a Senior Director - Operations you will be responsible for the performance of all operational functions of a large, complex location, or multiple remote locations. You will provide strategic leadership to meet and optimize established levels of business performance objectives, service, productivity, and quality. You will partner with leaders across supply chain, operations, and the business units to drive continuous improvement.

**Responsibilities:**

* Set strategic goals for operational efficiency and increased productivity.
* Lead team to ensure objectives are met, including driving customer service excellence plans, setting and managing performance targets, and employee performance management.
* Partner with Lean Leadership, ensuring LEAN methodologies are utilized and action plans are developed to correct problem areas and optimize established levels of business performance objectives, service, productivity, and quality
* Ensures consistent compliance with standard operating procedures, policies, internal audit controls, Sarbanes-Oxley controls, and business management quality system requirements
* Analyze current operational processes and performance, recommending solutions for improvement when necessary.
* Identifies market potential through competitor analysis and strategic planning.
* Develops annual business plans, identifies key activities, and priorities.
* Implements and communicates operational strategies and solutions consistent with business plans.
* Provides guidance to operations management in hiring and developing talent.
* Ensures operational excellence goals and audit requirements are met.
* Partners with inventory leaders to ensure region inventory needs and goals are met.
* Provides guidance to ensure business continuity and recovery plans are met.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelors degree preferred
* LEAN yellow belt certification
* 10+ years of operations leadership experience
* Experience running large, complex location or multiple remote locations
* Business and management principles, including strategic planning and resource allocation.
* Strategic thinking skills and ability to work with senior management and regional teams.
* Ability to streamline and implement new structures and roles that create speed, efficiency, and support rapidly shifting business demands
* In depth knowledge of diverse business functions and principles (e.g. supply chain, finance, customer service etc.)
* Working knowledge of data analysis and performance/operation metrics
* Strong decision-making and problem solving skills.
* Strong analytical skills.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to influence and lead change in a cross-functional team environment.
* Ability to travel 25% - 50% of the time.

 

Compensation Details $180,830 - $248,641 Annually

 

This amount is what we reasonably believe we will pay for the position; however, offer amounts may vary based on factors such as geographic location, relevant education, experience, qualifications, skills, shift, or any collective bargaining agreements.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 

Job Description:

The Senior Air Vehicle Operator (AVO) – Deployment Operations is responsible for executing and leading V-BAT flight operations in support of DoD and foreign customers in both land-based and maritime OCONUS environments. This is an operationally focused role requiring strong aviation judgment, disciplined execution, and the ability to lead small teams in austere and high-visibility conditions. 

 

The Senior AVO is responsible for leading mission planning activities, performing comprehensive risk assessments, delivering pre-mission briefings, executing flight operations, and conducting structured post-flight debriefs. This role includes conducting Functional Check Flights (FCFs) and system validation as required, ensuring aircraft configuration control and logbook accuracy, coordinating with maintenance to sustain fleet readiness, and supporting overall operational discipline. The Senior AVO will mentor junior operators, serve as the on-site operational representative to customers, and travel extensively in support of deployments. 

 

This is not an entry-level flight operations role. The ideal candidate brings strong aviation fundamentals, disciplined cockpit habits, and mature operational decision-making. They must be comfortable leading deployments, briefing customers, managing risk in dynamic environments, and maintaining professionalism in high-visibility settings. The Senior AVO must balance mission execution with customer satisfaction while upholding the highest standards of safety, compliance, and operational excellence. 

Required Qualifications:

 - Minimum of 2000 documented unmanned flight hours or 1000 manned flight hours 

 - Demonstrated instructor experience (manned or unmanned aviation)  

 - FAA Private Pilot License (PPL)  

 - FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate 

 - Ability to obtain and maintain an FAA Class II Medical Certificate 

 - Ability to obtain and hold a Secret DoD security clearance 

 - Ability to pass background, drug screening, and customer-required medical/dental screenings 

 - Willingness to travel up to 50–75% in support of deployments 

 - Ability to lead and operate independently in small teams under austere conditions 

 - Strong aviation judgment, decision-making, and risk management skills 

Preferred Qualifications

 - FAA Instrument Rating and/or Commercial Pilot License  

 - Experience operating as aircrew on manned aircraft  

 - Prior military service, particularly with overseas or deployed operations  

 - Maritime or shipboard UAS operational experience  

 - Previous experience as a Site Lead or in a leadership role overseeing aviation operations

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

At Shield AI, we’re building advanced autonomous aircraft that are redefining what is possible, and we are looking for a Staff Quality Engineer to help ensure our products meet the highest standards of performance, reliability, and safety. In this role, you will lead quality initiatives across the product lifecycle, driving improvements from early design and new product introduction through full-rate production.

 

You will be responsible for developing and maintaining robust quality systems in alignment with AS9100 standards, leading root cause investigations and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions. You will partner closely with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to identify risks, improve process capability, and ensure consistent product quality. Your work will include supporting NPI efforts, establishing control plans and inspection strategies, and using data-driven methods to monitor and improve manufacturing performance.


As a Staff Quality Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping quality strategy, mentoring team members, and influencing cross-functional decisions without direct authority. This is an opportunity to work hands on with next generation aerospace technology and contribute directly to the delivery of highly reliable autonomous systems that will define the future of aviation.

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)

 - 5+ years of experience in Quality, Manufacturing, or Process Engineering roles

 - Demonstrated experience leading root cause analysis and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions (RCA/CAPA)

 - Strong knowledge of quality systems and standards (AS9100 or similar)

 - Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI) and scaling production in a manufacturing environment

 - Proficiency in statistical analysis and process control methods (SPC, capability analysis, etc.)

 - Proven ability to work cross-functionally and influence engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams

Preferred qualifications:

 - Experience in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Lean Six Sigma certification, or equivalent

 - Knowledge of design for quality principles, including DFMEA, tolerance analysis, and design reviews

 - Experience working with quality and manufacturing systems (QMS, MES, PLM) and data analysis tools

 - Familiarity with advanced inspection or test methods (metrology, NDT, automated inspection, etc.)

Full-time regular employee offer package:

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

We are seeking a Senior Lead Operational Analyst to contribute to the modeling, simulation, and analysis of Shield AI’s aircraft systems. In this role, you will perform analysis at the component, system, mission and campaign levels to evaluate the effectiveness, survivability, and operational impact of our aircraft across multiple domains, missions and applications. You will collaborate closely with engineering, product, and defense stakeholders to assess system performance, inform design trade-offs, and improve mission outcomes. 


This position requires a strong working knowledge of military operations, modeling & simulation (M&S), data science, and operational analysis techniques. Your analyses will directly support product decisions and customer engagements by helping demonstrate how Shield AI’s AI-powered platforms perform in realistic and contested operational environments.

 - Engage with DoD stakeholders, operators, and analysts to understand mission needs and operational constraints.

 - Contribute to the development and refinement of concepts of operations (CONOPS) for AI-enabled aircraft capabilities.

 - Monitor emerging threats and operational challenges relevant to autonomous and air combat systems.

 - Prepare technical documentation, analysis reports, and briefings for internal teams, customers, and government stakeholders.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Mechatronics, or related STEM field. 

 - Experience in prototype manufacturing in a startup or rapid-growth environment.

Your responsibilities
 
 
**Lead Quality Excellence in a Fast-Paced Manufacturing Environment**
We are seeking an experienced
**Head of Quality**
to lead our Quality organization and drive world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing the Quality Management System, developing quality strategies, leading customer and supplier quality initiatives, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization.
 
 

* Lead and maintain the Quality Management System in compliance with IATF 16949 requirements.
* Develop and execute quality objectives, metrics, and improvement initiatives aligned with business goals.
* Manage customer and supplier quality activities, including audits, APQP, PPAP, launch readiness, corrective actions, and change management.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action efforts for internal and external quality issues.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Monitor and report key quality metrics, including scrap, rework, and overall quality performance.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to support production, new product launches, and supplier development.
* Build, develop, and lead high-performing quality teams.

**Success Competencies**
The Head of Quality embodies the following competencies:
 
 

* Manages Complexity: Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* Decision Quality: Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
* Action Oriented: Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy and enthusiasm.
* Ensures Accountability: Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments.
* Drive Results: Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.
* Develops Talent: Developing people to meet both their career goals and the organization’s goals.
* Builds Effective Teams: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspective to achieve common goals.
* Communicates Effectively: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* Instills Trust: Gaining the confidence and trust of others though honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
* Manages Ambiguity: Operating effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is not clear.
* Being Resilient: Rebounding from setbacks and adversity when facing difficult situations.

**Supervisory Responsibility:**
Directly manages the Quality Department including the Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, Quality Planning, Quality Lab/ Gauging, Change and Series Management functions.
 
 
Your profile
 
 
**Qualifications:**
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.
 
 

* Education: A Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or a related technical field is required, experience in Quality functions within the automotive industry or related areas.
* Language: Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers, OEMs, or employees of organization.
* Technology: Microsoft Office Suite knowledge; SAP/ERP knowledge preferred. Knowledge of IATF 16949, APQP-PPAP, FMEA, MSA, 8D, Statistics, GD&T and mechanical manufacturing processes.
* Travel: Occasional travel, up to 10% including international

**Group Presentation**

thyssenkrupp is an international industrial and technology group with more than 93,000 employees. In the fiscal year 2024/2025, the company generated sales of around €33 billion in 48 countries. Its business activities are bundled in five segments: Automotive Technology, Decarbon Technologies, Materials Services, Steel Europe and Marine Systems. With extensive technological know-how, outstanding engineering competence and a high level of innovative strength, the group develops solutions for the challenges of the future, especially in the fields of climate protection and energy transition, digital transformation in industry and mobility of the future.

To learn more about thyssenkrupp, please visit the following link: thyssenkrupp As An Employer - North America

**Company Presentation**

thyssenkrupp Dynamic Components is one of the world's automotive industry leading partners for development and manufacturing of highly complex, state-of-the-art drivetrain technologies for both combustion engines and electric motors. Worldwide, 10 locations with 3,800 employees produce over 25 million drivetrain components per year. The product portfolio includes camshafts and cylinder head cover modules for the valve train as well as rotor shafts for battery electric vehicles.

Our electrical A/C compressor, designed for the natural refrigerant CO
*2*
, sets new standards in efficient and sustainable thermal management.

With precision and passion, we are enabling our customers in the automotive industry to achieve their emission and sustainability targets for more than 30 years.

thyssenkrupp Presta Dynamic Components is proud to be Certified™ by
**Great Place To Work®**
. The prestigious award is based entirely on what current employees say about their experience working at thyssenkrupp Presta Dynamic Components. This year, 82% of employees said it's a great place To Work - 25 points higher than the average U.S. company. Great Place To Work® is the global authority on workplace culture, employee experience, and the leadership behaviors proven to deliver market-leading revenue, employee retention and increased innovation.

**Your Responsibilities**

**Lead Quality Excellence in a Fast-Paced Manufacturing Environment**

We are seeking an experienced

**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264447 **Date posted** 16/11/2026

 

**Introduction**

As Senior Director, CMC Product Lead and Head of Product Stewardship, you will lead end-to-end CMC product strategy and the Product Stewardship and Product Champion organization within Global Technical Operations (GTO).

You will lead sophisticated Global CMC programs across development, PPQ, commercialization, and lifecycle management while shaping Product Stewardship capabilities, governance, processes, and talent.

You will guide strategy, manage risk, and drive cross-functional decisions that support product progression and commercial supply.

**What you'll do**

You will lead global CMC operations groups for sophisticated biologics and other advanced modalities across development, PPQ, market rollout, and end-to-end product stewardship. You will define and deliver Global CMC strategies across manufacturing science and technology, manufacturing, analytical, quality, regulatory, technical transfer, and supply activities.

You will lead all aspects of the responsibilities related to Product Stewardship and the role of Product Champion, improving technical and CMC leadership throughout the product lifecycle. Working with BPD, Cross-SET, eGPT, GPT, and Operations teams, you will shape product strategy, influence decisions, and resolve cross-functional issues. Ensure products and processes are scalable, robust, transferable, and ready for commercialization and lifecycle management.

You will advance Early Engagement and drive CoGS strategy, identifying risks early and incorporating yield, process efficiency, manufacturability, network fit, and supply resilience into product decisions. You will also strengthen post-launch CMC leadership across product quality, supply, lifecycle improvements, and post-approval submissions.

You will establish effective governance, decision rights, escalation pathways, role clarity, and ways of working. You will lead all aspects of sophisticated product, technical, quality, supply, and CMC issues and represent Operations, Biologics, and GTO in senior governance discussions.

You will champion data-driven decision-making and the practical use of digital tools, sophisticated analytics, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities. You will build organizational strength through talent development, succession planning, and an inclusive, high-performing culture.

**Essential requirements**

* Degree in a relevant scientific or engineering field.
* 15+ years of leadership experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with deep expertise in biologics, CMC, technical operations, commercialization, product stewardship, or related fields.
* Experience leading sophisticated Global CMC programs, Operations Global CMC teams, major biologics products, or comparable cross-functional technical programs.
* Strong understanding of late-stage development, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation and PPQ, commercialization, control strategy, comparability, lifecycle management, and post-approval change.
* Proven track record to align cross-functional teams within a global matrix.
* Experience leading senior technical teams and building organizational capability through talent development and succession planning.
* Strong enterprise and matrix leadership, with the credibility to influence decisions in senior governance forums.
* Excellent communication and judgment, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly and connect technical decisions with product and business outcomes.

**Desirable requirements**

* Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or engineering field.
* Experience leading Product Stewardship, Product Champion, technical product leadership, or similar product-facing organizations.
* Experience across development and commercial manufacturing networks, including internal and external supply.
* Experience with Global CMC governance, regulatory submissions, post-approval change

record.ROLE_TEXT:
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day operations at Innova's M3 facility in Mexicali, Mexico, including production, maintenance, purchasing, shipping and receiving, and site safety. Working closely with the site leadership team, this role ensures production goals, quality standards, cost targets, and customer delivery commitments are met. The Director builds and develops a strong local team, drives continuous improvement, and serves as the key link between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Finance, Quality, and Sales teams. The ideal candidate is based in the San Diego area, is fully bilingual in English and Spanish, and has proven experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Champion and uphold the company's values, mission, and quality policy in all activities.

* Adhere to and help enforce company policies, procedures, and internal control standards.

* Ensure compliance with all applicable Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Follow all safety rules and PPE requirements, and promptly report hazards, incidents, and near-misses.

* Lead all operations at the M3 facility, including production, maintenance, purchasing, and shipping and receiving, to meet production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery commitments.

* Direct and develop the site leadership team, including hiring, training, performance management, and succession planning.

* Oversee production planning and scheduling to balance capacity, labor, and materials with customer demand.

* Establish operational KPIs and monitor productivity, efficiency, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery, taking corrective action as needed.

* Oversee the site safety program and ensure compliance with applicable Mexican health, safety, and environmental regulations (e.g., STPS and NOM standards), fostering a strong culture of safety.

* Develop and manage the site operating budget, labor plan, and capital expenditure requests.

* Oversee equipment maintenance and facility upkeep to maximize uptime and maintain a safe, organized plant.

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve throughput, and lower costs.

* Coordinate with logistics and customs partners to support cross-border shipments, materials flow, and import/export requirements.

* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations, and compliance with Mexican labor law.

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Quality, Finance, and Sales, providing regular operational and financial reporting.

* Perform other related duties as required.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, required.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico (maquiladora or similar cross-border environment) strongly preferred.

* Experience with plastics manufacturing processes (e.g., injection molding, thermoforming, CNC machining) preferred.

* Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification preferred.

**SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) required.

* Proven leadership skills, with the ability to build, motivate, and develop a high-performing team.

* Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, and plant management.

* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.

* Financial acumen, with the ability to develop budgets, manage costs, and interpret financial data.

* Working knowledge of Mexican labor, safety, and environmental regulations.

* Working knowledge of quality system requirements under ISO 90

**We're looking for a**

**Director, Product Operations**
================================

**This role is** **Hybrid, Dublin Office**

The **Director, Product Operations** is a senior leader who improves how the product development organization makes decisions and turns strategy into results. This role strengthens portfolio planning and execution while connecting product investments to customer and business outcomes.

Working across functions and through influence, the Director brings clarity to complex choices, aligns senior stakeholders, and drives accountability for outcomes. The role helps leaders make timely tradeoffs, improves execution predictability, and ensures product investments deliver measurable value.

**\*\*Preference for candidate who can be hybrid in Dublin, CA or Santa Monica, CA or New York office**

**In this role you will…**
--------------------------

### **Product Operating Model and Operational Rigor**

* Establish and continuously improve the product operating model, including planning cycles, portfolio and roadmap reviews, decision forums, product performance reviews, and post-launch learning loops, with a focus on improving decision quality, speed, accountability, and measurable outcomes.
* Create integrated visibility into priorities, milestones, dependencies, capacity, risks, decisions, and commitments across the product portfolio.
* Drive disciplined follow-through on decisions and actions, surfacing tradeoffs and gaps early and ensuring accountable owners are aligned.

### **Portfolio Strategy and Investment Planning**

* Partner with Product, Engineering, and Finance leaders to translate company and product strategy into a balanced, executable portfolio of investments.
* Implement a horizon-based planning approach that balances near-term customer and commercial commitments, core product and platform health, and longer-term growth and innovation.
* Connect portfolio choices to expected customer, product, operational, and financial outcomes, with clear assumptions, capacity implications, dependencies, and risks.

### **Product Intelligence and Executive Decision Support**

* Integrate customer feedback, product usage, market signals, delivery performance, and financial data to identify trends, evaluate portfolio performance, and inform product decisions.
* Provide senior leaders with concise, data-driven insights and recommendations that frame portfolio choices, investment tradeoffs, performance gaps, and decisions requiring leadership action.
* Translate complex and sometimes conflicting inputs into clear options, implications, and recommended actions that improve decision quality and accelerate alignment.

### **Delivery Success and Value Realization**

* Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to establish measurable success criteria and outcome targets before major investments and roadmap commitments are approved.
* Promote delivery practices that prioritize customer value, adoption, retention, quality, supportability, and business impact over feature output alone.
* Identify barriers to value realization and coordinate the cross-functional actions needed to improve enablement, readiness, adoption, product performance, or customer outcomes.

**You have what it takes if…**
------------------------------

* 8+ years of progressive experience in Product Operations, Product Management, Business Operations, Strategy, Program Management, Finance, or a related function within a complex technology or SaaS organization.
* Demonstrated success establishing or scaling product planning, portfolio management, governance, analytics, or operating rhythms across Product and Engineering organizations.
* Experience guiding portfolio prioritization and investment tradeoffs across customer, strategic, technical, operational, and financial needs.
* Strong understanding of product development lifecycles, roadmap planning, release execution, adoption, and post-launch value realization.

With a vision rooted in the wellbeing and inclusive engagement of our team members, our customers, their end users and our communities, people are the heart of what we do and who we are. It is our values that unite us and guide us in everything that we do, including how we operate, behave and interact to foster a workplace where every team member feels valued and empowered to contribute their best.
 
 
Our values include: Growing our People, Building Belonging, Innovating Responsibly, Delivering Excellence and Creating Customer Success.
 
 
As a team member, you will engage in impactful work through global collaboration and the use of emerging technologies, join an inclusive culture where every team member is valued and working toward a greater purpose, and be empowered to reach your full potential through various development programs designed to accelerate your growth.
 
 
Plexus offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support team members' wellbeing, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, retirement savings, and opportunities for professional development. $132,500.00 - $198,700.00

To provide leadership and direction to the Manufacturing Engineering team(s) from a functional perspective. Manage the Manufacturing Engineering function in line with functional specific strategies, process and systems development, people development, employee relations, plant level metrics.

* Lead manufacturing-engineering excellence by collaborating with various functional leads to ensure engineering capability meets or exceeds manufacturing standards for quality product delivery.
* Support Program Management initiatives and activities to meet or exceed customer expectations.
* Lead process/product/equipment engineering activities in compliance with Plexus Core Values to meet industry standards, regulatory and customer requirements.
* Provide technical leadership to site operations, establish a technology roadmap, and collaborate with corporate and regional technical teams to achieve lower costs and higher manufacturing returns.

* Bachelor’s Degree with 8 or more years of related experience is preferred. An equivalent combination of education and/or experience will be considered.
* Proven leadership skills and management experience.
