------------------------

This role represents a critical executive leadership opportunity for a dynamic Director of Operations – Chillers to join the Global Operations team. Reporting directly to the VP of Global Operations with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President & General Manager (VPGM) of the Chillers business unit, this leader has direct operational responsibility for all global chiller manufacturing plants.

Each global chiller facility holds full SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) execution accountability. To drive self-sufficient, world-class execution at the plant level, the Director of Operations – Chillers will lead a comprehensive, multi-functional organization where each plant team includes dedicated Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations resources.

As an integral member of the Global Operations team, this individual operates as an influential peer to Supply Chain (partnering to enable global Supply Chain and SIOP execution) and Materials (partnering to enable Materials management and Localized Procurement strategies), as well as the broader Global Operations leadership team. By bridging global functional capabilities with plant-level execution and business unit strategy, the Director of Operations – Chillers will drive rapid operational transformation, capacity expansion, and sustainable business growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **1. Global Plant Leadership & SQDC Execution Accountability**

* Hold direct operational oversight and P&L/conversion cost accountability for all global chiller manufacturing facilities.
* Drive rigorousSQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) daily management and execution across every chiller site:

* **Safety:** Champion a zero-injury culture, ensuring proactive EHS compliance, ergonomic improvements, and behavioral safety leadership across all plants.
* **Quality:** Ensure zero-defect manufacturing standards, robust quality management systems, customer compliance, and rapid root-cause corrective actions.
* **Delivery:** Achieve industry-leading on-time delivery (OTD) and lead-time competitiveness through effective line balancing, capacity tracking, and constraint management.
* **Cost:** Optimize direct and indirect labor productivity, overhead absorption, scrap reduction, and continuous conversion cost improvements.

### **2. Multi-Functional Team Management & Talent Development**

* Lead, mentor, and develop Plant Managers and site leadership teams across the global chiller footprint.
* Ensure each plant's respective organization is effectively structured and resourced across Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations to deliver autonomous day-to-day SQDC execution.
* Build organizational capability, establish clear succession plans, and foster an empowered, high-accountability, results-oriented culture across both salaried and direct labor workforces.

**Job Responsibilities Continued**
----------------------------------

**Position:** Director – Operations 
**Location:** North Carolina/ South Carolina 
**Type:** Full-Time 
**Reports To:** CEO, ZetSol Energy

**Who We Are**

ZetSol Energy is the solar manufacturing and supply chain platform built to give North American solar developers, EPCs, utilities, and independent power producers a reliable, tariff-compliant alternative to fragmented overseas sourcing. The company is establishing a vertically integrated greenfield facility in Tuticorin, Tamil Nadu, producing silicon ingots, monocrystalline wafers, cells, and modules, including high-efficiency TOPCon and HJT technology, and pairs that manufacturing base with a full strategic sourcing, bill-of-materials management, quality audit, compliance, and logistics practice purpose-built for the US market.

ZetSol Energy is backed by Zetwerk, a global manufacturing platform valued at over $2.7 billion that already supplies solar piles, mechanical and structural components, and modules to leading US EPCs and asset owners, and whose 2022 acquisition of Unimacts strengthened its US industrial and solar manufacturing footprint. ZetSol Energy is the next chapter of that build-out: a dedicated US-facing commercial platform launching at a moment when American solar developers are actively searching for supply chain partners who can deliver both scale and certainty.

**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced operations leader to lead and scale ZetSol Energy's US operations, with overall responsibility for manufacturing, factory production, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in managing large-scale operations, with a strong background in Supply Chain Management (SCM), logistics and manufacturing, preferably within the renewable energy, solar or industrial sectors.

This individual will be responsible for overseeing factory production, managing end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, and driving sales operations, including demand planning, order management and customer fulfilment in the US market.

The role will also involve building strong relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, logistics partners and other key industry stakeholders, while ensuring operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and cost optimisation.

This is a key leadership position that will play an instrumental role in building and scaling ZetSol Energy's US operations, establishing robust operational processes and driving business growth in North America.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead and oversee end-to-end US operations for ZetSol Energy, covering manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.

* Manage factory production operations, including production planning, capacity utilisation, quality, productivity and timely delivery.

* Drive end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, including global sourcing, procurement, inventory management, import/export, customs clearance and distribution.

* Oversee sales operations, including demand planning, order management, customer fulfilment and coordination with commercial teams.

* Build and manage relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities, logistics partners and other key stakeholders.

* Ensure compliance with US trade regulations, import policies, tariffs and applicable industry standards while driving operational efficiency and cost optimisation.

* Build and scale the US operations team, processes and infrastructure while working closely with the leadership and manufacturing teams in India.

**Qualifications**

* 15–20 years of experience in operations, manufacturing, supply chain management and logistics, preferably within renewable energy, solar, infrastructure or industrial sectors.

* Extensive experience managing large-scale manufacturing operations, including factory production, production planning, quality and operational efficiency.

* Strong exp

The Regional Operations Director leads regional performance by aligning people, processes, and financial priorities with business goals. You’ll guide operations across the region, strengthen customer service, and use clear, data-driven decisions to improve results. * Lead regional operations, business management, and strategic planning; translate priorities into clear plans and accountable execution.

* Identify opportunities for process improvement and apply lean management principles to strengthen operational management and performance.

* Demonstrated leadership, management, and supervising experience in operations or business management.
* Experience with financial management, P&L oversight, and data-driven decision making.
* Ability to lead managers, develop teams, communicate with executives, and coordinate cross-functional projects.
* Knowledge of strategic management, sales, customer service, and process improvement; experience applying lean management principles is preferred.
* Strong analytical and organizational skills, including proficiency in Excel data analysis.

Pay: $73,200.00 - $88,300.00 per year

Benefits:

* Employee discount
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Health savings account

As a Regional Operations Director, you are a key leader responsible for the success and health of a diverse portfolio of veterinary hospitals. You will serve as the crucial link between local hospital teams and the broader Mission Pet Health network, empowering your teams to achieve excellence in both business performance and patient care.

Ideal candidates will reside within the greater Chicago metropolitan area or surrounding communities, with the ability to travel regularly throughout the assigned hospital portfolio. * **Develop Future Leaders:** You'll guide the growth of Hospital Managers and their teams, ensuring a strong pipeline of talent through effective coaching, training, and career development.
* **Drive Business Performance:** You'll have full ownership of the financial health of your region, managing P&Ls to drive revenue growth and optimize operational efficiency.
* **Build Winning Teams:** You'll lead the strategy for non-DVM recruiting and staffing, ensuring your hospitals have the talent they need to succeed.
* **Elevate the Client Experience:** You'll set the standard for exceptional client service, ensuring operational processes support a seamless and positive experience for every pet owner.

### **What You'll Bring to the Team**

* A proven track record of successful multi-site P&L management, with a keen ability to drive financial results.

* Exceptional leadership skills with a talent for building a positive, accountable, and solutions-focused culture.
* Excellent communication and conflict management skills, with the ability to tailor messages to diverse audiences.
* Significant experience leading in a multi-site veterinary, healthcare, or customer-centric retail environment.

### **How You're Supported**

*As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.* 
 
*Note: Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage. Eligibility for specific benefits varies based on your role and hours worked.*

##### **Competitive Compensation**

A competitive hourly rate or salary based on your experience and role.

##### **Health & Wellbeing**

We offer comprehensive coverage options including Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, along with access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for all teammates.

##### **Financial Security**

Plan for your future with our 401k retirement options and additional financial protection benefits like Life Insurance and Disability coverage.

##### **Commitment to Growth**

We support your career goals with opportunities for professional development, including educational assistance for qualified teammates to enroll in AVMA-accredited veterinary technician programs.

##### **The Power of a Network**

Join a nationwide community of over 20,000 veterinary professionals who share a passion for collaboration, career growth, and sharing best practices.

##### **Valuable Perks**

Enjoy discounted veterinary care for your own pets, access to an online discount platform, and free 24/7 access to doctors through Teladoc.

**The Team:** 
The Hermès Palm Beach Boutique opened in 1977 and focuses on providing extraordinary service to clients as a part of the Southern Region. This position will report to the Managing Director and will work collaboratively with the sales team and selling support teams to support the client experience in a fast-paced, luxury environment.

**The Opportunity:** 
The Operations Director is responsible for overseeing all operational functions which may include inventory control, housekeeping, maintenance and selling service associates. This position is responsible for adhering to P&L budget for all operational areas. The Director of Operations communicates trains and implements all company policies and ensures compliance. The Operations Director will create efficient processes, set parameters and implement directives to support operational efficiency and growth.

All other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

**About the Role:**

* Manages shipping and receiving department. Assess actions to be taken with receiving issues. Ensure the timely movement of merchandise and adherence to all procedural guidelines including but not limited to transfers, RTVs, damages, negative on hands etc. Through management of inventory control associates and other operational staff, ensure the organization and efficient operation of all back of house space.
* Takes part in all managerial responsibilities for efficient running of the business inclusive of overseeing and validating cash handling procedures are respected, appropriately documented and reported to Managing Director. Operations Director will contribute and work in tandem with retail management team as needed and in fair rotation. Operations Director will also assist in the absence of Managing Director and Floor Directors during Podium, vacations or in the absence of the Assistant Manager or Selling Supervisor.
* Ensure workflow of all after-sales service and craftspeople/tailors if applicable.
* Performs and prepares for all inventories and cycle counts, including reconciliations of stock discrepancies. Performs stock adjustments.
* Liaison with corporate construction and maintenance department and outside vendors with regards to any maintenance needs. Ensure building and store are maintained to company standard and all issues are addressed in a timely manner.
* Ensure functionality of all IT and phone system by communicating with corporate contacts and securing resolutions.
* Acts as a liaison with outside vendors for monthly need and or special events.
* Partners with Managing Director to manage operational team and vendors ensuring appropriate scheduling training and coaching. Manages E-time and keeps accurate record of vacation and time and attendance with HR. This includes all SSA’s, housekeeping, shipping and receiving, asset protection guards and after sales staff as appropriate for the location.
* Coordinates and prepares evacuation drills and provides training to team with regards to emergency response preparedness.
* Responsible for and oversees all operations and after-sales supply orders.
* Oversees all Staff Sales
* Trains staffs to ensure compliance with all operational policies and procedures ensuring policies are thoroughly communicated to all staff in a timely manner.
Recruits and maintains an active talent bank for any operational positions. 

**Supervisory Responsibility:**

* YES

Supervises Inventory Control, SSA and After-Sales positions. (Tailor, Maintenance, Crafts persons)

**Budget Responsibility:**

* YES

Budget guidelines are set annually. The Operations Director will be directly involved with budget expectations with regards to selling supplies, cleaning and maintenance contracts, guard service, repairs, rental equipment and kitchen supplies. They will work within the confines of the budget in partnership with the respective corporate departments. The Operations Director should identify areas for cost efficient and minimize costs when possible.

**Discover your future at Citi**
--------------------------------

Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.

**Job Overview**
----------------

This Managing Director role, Global Head of Custody Operations and NAM Lead for Investor Services Operations, is a senior leadership position within the Investor Services Operations leadership team, reporting within Services Operations.

The role provides global strategic accountability for Citi's Custody Operations franchise and senior leadership accountability for North America (NAM) Investor Services Operations, including institutional governance, regulatory compliance, and market-leading asset safety across multi-trillion-dollar traditional and emerging asset portfolios.

The successful candidate will set the strategic vision and deliver the multi-year transformation roadmap across Citi's Custody franchise, spanning international branch operations and shared service hubs, while leading an international workforce of approximately 1,700 professionals across more than 60 countries. This includes oversight of the global operating model, direct custody market access, sub-custody networks, and core post-trade infrastructure

The role requires close partnership with Technology, Product Management, Sales, Markets, Risk, Legal, Audit, and business leadership to ensure Citi maintains a best-in-class custody control environment and resilient investor services infrastructure while supporting commercial growth. The position demands significant experience leading large-scale global operations organizations within highly regulated environments and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across businesses, functions, geographies, regulators, and industry bodies.

 
 

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic & Operational Leadership:**

 
 

* Lead the Custody Operations organization, delivering operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and strong client outcomes.
* Provide senior leadership and oversight for NAM Investor Services Operations, ensuring resilient, timely, and effective execution across critical custody and investor servicing activities.
* Architect and execute the global Target Operating Model (TOM), strategically balancing scale across centralized multi-hub Centers of Excellence with direct custody market access across 60+ countries.
* Define and execute the strategic vision for Custody Operations and NAM Investor Services Operations, aligning operational priorities with Citi's business, risk, client, and regulatory objectives.
* Drive transformation initiatives that improve effectiveness, scalability, resilience, productivity, and service quality.
* Sponsor enterprise post-trade technology investments, steering legacy platform rationalization and the transition to cloud-native, API-first, and event-driven market connectivity.
* Partner across Operations, Technology, Product, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Audit, and business leadership to deliver strategic priorities and enterprise objectives.

* Maintain end-to-end accountability for Custody operations, including settlement, asset servicing, income processing, and related operational activities across traditional and emerging asset classes.
* Ensure effective execution of custody controls across sub-custody networks, direct market access arrangements, and shared service hubs.

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
 
 
**POSTING TIMELINE**

ZetSol Energy is the solar manufacturing and supply chain platform built to give North American solar developers, EPCs, utilities, and independent power producers a reliable, tariff-compliant alternative to fragmented overseas sourcing.

The company is establishing a vertically integrated greenfield facility in Tuticorin, Tamil Nadu, producing silicon ingots, monocrystalline wafers, cells, and modules, including high-efficiency TOPCon and HJT technology, and pairs that manufacturing base with a full strategic sourcing, bill-of-materials management, quality audit, compliance, and logistics practice purpose-built for the US market.

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Role Description**
The Vice President of Quality Assurance is a senior, full-time remote role responsible for leading the quality vision, strategy, and execution across Allianz Trade’s operations. This position oversees the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality assurance frameworks, policies, and procedures to ensure consistent service delivery and compliance with internal standards and external regulations. Day-to-day tasks include directing quality audits, monitoring quality performance metrics, identifying root causes of issues, and driving corrective and preventive actions in partnership with cross-functional leaders. The role involves collaborating with operations, technology, compliance, and risk management teams to embed quality best practices into processes, systems, and customer interactions. The Vice President will also guide and mentor quality teams, manage departmental budgets, and report on quality objectives, outcomes, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership.

**Qualifications**

* Strong background in Quality Assurance and Quality Control, with demonstrated experience designing and leading enterprise-wide quality programs.
* Expertise in Quality Management and Quality Auditing, including setting performance standards, conducting audits, and implementing continuous improvement initiatives.
* Solid understanding of Regulatory Requirements relevant to financial services or insurance, with the ability to translate regulatory expectations into practical quality controls.
* Proven leadership experience in senior quality or operational roles, including managing teams, influencing stakeholders, and driving change across complex organizations.
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with proficiency in using data and metrics to evaluate performance and prioritize improvements.
* Strong communication and collaboration abilities, including presenting to executive audiences and partnering effectively with global and cross-functional teams in a remote environment.
* Relevant academic background, such as a bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, operations, engineering, quality management, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., Six Sigma, ISO, CQE/CQA) are a plus.
* Experience within insurance, financial services, or risk management industries is highly beneficial, along with familiarity with digital tools and enterprise quality systems.

The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact.
 
 
**Locations**
Stanford Health Care

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

**Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities**

* Must have strong leadership and interpersonal skills and be effective at people management including the ability to delegate assignments and share decision-making with team members and direct reports as appropriate.
* Excellent communication skills including the ability to present, and to write in a clear and understandable manner.
* Ability to understand complex verbal or written instructions and translate to action to deliver quantitative and qualitative results.
* Must be well organized and systematic, and able to design, implement and maintain standard work processes.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies to lead complex project teams and large scope projects, including managing resources (people, costs, time).

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.

Job Summary

The Director of Compliance provides strategic and operational leadership for critical compliance activities across the medical device organization. This role leads regulatory inspection readiness, product issue escalation and compliance risk assessment, regulatory agency responses, correction and removal activities, and large-scale compliance improvement initiatives.
 
 
The Director serves as a senior compliance partner to Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, and business leadership, ensuring significant quality and compliance issues are rapidly assessed, appropriately escalated, and effectively resolved. The position requires strong judgment, executive communication, and the ability to lead complex, cross-functional activities in a highly regulated environment.
 
 
Beyond compliance subject-matter leadership, the Director owns the compliance function's budget and resourcing, shapes its organizational strategy and structure, and contributes to broader business planning — balancing business objectives with compliance risk and representing the function in strategic and operational business reviews. The Director leads a global team of regional compliance specialists, building organizational capability across all manufacturing sites and functions.



**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

Organizational Strategy & Business Leadership

* Shape the multi-year strategy and organizational design for the compliance function, including workforce planning, capability building, and succession planning.

* Lead, develop, and manage a global team of compliance professionals, including direct oversight of regional compliance specialists across manufacturing sites.

* Partner with business, Quality, and Regulatory leadership to align compliance priorities with broader business strategy, product roadmaps, and operational plans.

* Represent the compliance organization in business planning, budget reviews, and strategic planning forums, providing a compliance-risk perspective to business decisions.

* Build organizational capability and structure to scale the compliance function as the business grows.

Inspection Readiness

* Establish and maintain an enterprise inspection-readiness program supporting regulatory inspections and other external assessments.

* Lead inspection preparation, including readiness assessments, mock inspections, documentation reviews, front-room/back-room preparation, subject-matter-expert coaching, and inspection logistics.

* Identify systemic readiness gaps and drive corrective actions to improve sustained inspection preparedness.

* Develop inspection-readiness metrics, lessons learned, and continuous-improvement mechanisms.

Product Issue Escalation & Risk Assessment

* Lead or facilitate cross-functional assessments of significant product quality, safety, compliance, and regulatory issues requiring senior-level escalation.

* Ensure emerging product issues are evaluated using structured, documented risk-based decision-making.

* Partner with Medical Safety, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, Operations, and other functions to evaluate product and compliance risk and determine appropriate escalation and response.

* Provide independent compliance challenge and guidance when significant product-related decisions could create regulatory or patient-safety implications.

* Ensure escalated issues have clear ownership, documented rationale, timely decisions, and appropriate executive visibility.

Regulatory Agency Responses

* Lead the development and coordination of responses to regulatory inspection observations, agency inquiries, compliance correspondence, and other significant regulatory matters.

* Establish cross-functional response teams, governance, deliverables, and escalation mechanisms.

* Ensure responses are factually supported, internally consistent, appropriately reviewed, and supported by sustainable corrective actions.

Duties Description Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center (KFPC), an Office of Mental Health (OMH) secure forensic facility, is recruiting a Deputy Director, Psychiatric Center 1 - Quality Management (DDPC 1 - QM) to oversee their Quality Management Program.
 
 
The DDPC 1 - QM is an essential member of the facility's Executive Management Team. Under the general direction of the Executive Director and in close collaboration with the facility leadership team at KFPC, the DDPC 1 – QM participates in developing, implementing, interpreting, and evaluating the facility's mission, goals, and policies and how they impact the care and clinical treatment provided to the adults, youth, and families they serve.
 
 
The DDPC 1 – QM is responsible for:
 

* Supervising all departments assigned to the Quality Management Program - program evaluation, risk management, utilization review, health information management, and staff development.
* Ensuring compliance with OMH, The Joint Commission (TJC), the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and external regulatory agencies standards, cultural competence, and continuous quality improvement.
* Ensuring high-quality and effective care in both inpatient and outpatient programs.

Minimum Qualifications Minimum Qualifications:
 
 
A. Education
 
 
A master’s degree in a mental hygiene discipline, hospital or health administration, or other administrative area specifically related to health care, sociology, statistics, or quantitative research; or a license to practice medicine in New York State or Canada.
 
 
AND
 
 
B. Experience
 
 
Six (6) years of experience in a mental health program or health care setting that includes one of the following:
 
 
1. Four (4) years of managerial experience in one quality management component area, such as program evaluation, clinical risk management, standards compliance, survey readiness, utilization review, or a closely related area; or
 
2. Three (3) years of managerial experience in two of the above quality management component areas; or
 
3. Two (2) years of managerial experience in three of the above quality management component areas.

Additional Comments About KFPC
 
KFPC, located on Ward’s Island in New York City, provides inpatient treatment and rehabilitation to pretrial defendants who were deemed unfit to stand trial and were court ordered for restoration of fitness to stand trial and individuals who have been found not guilty by reason of insanity.
 
 
KFPC is committed to supporting underserved individuals and delivering treatment with respect for each individual's privacy and rights along with activities and initiatives to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment for underserved populations.
 
 
About OMH
 
OMH operates the largest state mental health system in the country, with 23 hospitals, 90 clinics, two world-class research institutes, a secure residential center, and a network of community services. OMH hospitals are all Joint Commission-accredited and recognized as among the best mental health hospital systems in the United States. OMH believes everyone should have an equal opportunity to achieve mental wellness. This means implementing services and policies to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment outcomes for historically marginalized, underserved, and unserved populations.
 
 
If you would like to join KFPC and contribute to a workforce dedicated to public service, we offer:
 

* Generous paid time off, including thirteen (13) vacation days, eight (8) sick days, and five (5) personal days accrued during the first year of employment; thirteen (13) paid holidays each year.
* Option to choose a NYS health insurance plan that meets your needs.
* Dental and vision coverage.
* Enrollment in the New York State and Local Retirement System (NYSLRS) or a voluntary defined contribution plan.

 
The posted salary includes the Downstate Adjustment of $4,150.

Responsibilities:

The Director, Compliance, Quality & Risk Management provides enterprise-wide strategic and operational leadership for the Foundation’s compliance, organizational quality, and enterprise risk management functions. 
The Director is accountable for establishing and maintaining integrated frameworks, governance processes, and performance standards that strengthen organizational accountability, regulatory compliance, operational effectiveness, and proactive risk management across Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation. The Director owns the enterprise risk management framework, leads enterprise quality improvement and compliance oversight, and partners with executive and operational leaders to identify systemic risks, establish organizational standards, and drive measurable improvements. The Director provides leadership across a complex, multi-state healthcare organization, translating regulatory requirements, organizational risks, and performance insights into actionable strategies that advance the Foundation’s mission, operational integrity, and long-term sustainability.
 
 
This role strengthens Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation’s ability to manage regulatory complexity, maintain consistent quality standards, identify enterprise risks, and provide coordinated oversight across a geographically dispersed organization. Through integrated governance and disciplined execution, the Director helps protect the Foundation’s mission, supports organizational sustainability, and advances the delivery of safe, ethical, high-quality services.

* Quality Management and Continuous Improvement
* Enterprise Risk Management and Patient Safety

* Demonstrated sound judgment, professional integrity, and ability to handle sensitive or confidential matters.

* Advanced degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, law, or a related field.

* Experience leading organizational transformation or consolidating multiple functions

Cenveo is a leading North American manufacturer of envelopes with over 100 years of experience and approximately 30 billion envelopes manufactured annually. We are committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence.

We are hiring immediately for an experienced Plant Manager for its envelope manufacturing facility in Chicago, IL. The position will report into the Site-Leader/General Manager.

Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, Cenveo provides competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager directs the manufacturing, maintenance, warehousing and distribution operations of a facility to achieve business goals including safety, quality, and production (including efficiency and profitability). They ensure compliance with all government regulations and corporate policies. Additionally, the Plant Manager serves as a liaison between the manufacturing facility and its clients, the Sales department, and other groups.

**Key Responsibilities** (\*Essential Functions)

*These are functions a qualified incumbent or applicant must be able to perform with or without reasonable accommodation.*

* Through direct action and the management of others, ensure the safe, productive, and profitable daily operations of an envelope manufacturing facility.
* Effectively use financial, & other, reports to monitor and improve facility performance on a variety of business related metrics. Prepare similar reports as required.
* Select, train, and develop subordinates necessary to conduct facility operations.
* Direct the plant supervision team in the enforcement and consistent application of policies, and plant rules which may include the terms of a collective bargaining agreement.
* Monitor, train and communicate safety and quality programs and ensure compliance with company policies and government regulations.
* Ensure the efficient and effective purchasing and utilization of all materials and services.
* Collaborate with sales to improve or modify existing products as needed, and to aid in new product development.
* Visit customer facilities, or host customer visits to the Cenveo facility to aid in sales, customer relations, or the resolution of problem situations.
* Monitor new trends and developments in business and manufacturing.
* Represent the company and facility in community relations functions.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Perform other duties as assigned based on business needs.

**Pay / Other**

* Salaried Pay Range: $120,000 – 140,000 annually
* Schedule: Monday – Friday; Saturdays required during peak production/business needs.

**Other (Non-Essential) Functions**

Includes functions which are normally performed by persons holding this title. However, these functions may be reassigned to other employees as part of a "Reasonable Accommodation" under the ADA.

* Other duties and assignments as required.

**Job Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree preferred. Will consider experience in lieu of Bachelor's degree, emphasis on Manufacturing, Industrial Management, or similar preferred.
* Comprehensive experience in manufacturing, along with advanced knowledge in multiple related disciplines and processes is required.
* Experience in envelope, printing or packaging is highly preferred.
* Extensive experience Environmental, Health, & Safety.
* Six Sigma / Lean Manufacturing experience preferred.
* Managing teams or projects is preferred.
* Strong PC skills including Microsoft Office and internet research
* Strong interpersonal verbal and written communication
* Ability to work independently and with others, demonstrate analytical abilities, and be a strong and versatile leader.
* Must be a self-starter and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
* Ability to perform work, and resolve problems, that are complex and varied in nature.

* Complete and turn in all paperwork and log in a professional, legible, and timely manner.
* Manage aggregate production to ensure goals and objectives are met.
* Responsible for maintenance and repair of all mobile and stationary equipment.
* Ensures that the workforce complies with policies, procedures, and regulations to produce a productive labor climate at plant facilities.
* Assist Plant Managers and Quality Control Departments as necessary to ensure quality products, accounts & service.
* Assist in development of riverbed aggregate sites, pit operations and reclamation.
* Equipment repair and preventative maintenance
* Interact with vendors and employees.
* Maintain a high degree of customers satisfaction and employee morale through problem solving.
* Ensure a safe working environment through daily inspections and monthly safety meetings.
* Supervise 1-2 aggregate plants (both fixed and mobile)

* High School diploma or equivalent
* A minimum of 5 years’ experience in the operations of a sand and gravel pit.
* Experience in a supervisory capacity
* Knowledge of MSHA rules and regulations

* Ability to understand and follow instructions.
* Ability to learn the methods and practices used in our business.
* Ability to perform strenuous work in varying weather conditions.
* Knowledge of heavy equipment including but not limited to loaders, dozers, and hydraulic excavators and off-road haul trucks. **Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for leading and optimizing all aspects of business unit operations (water, wastewater and natural gas) to achieve exceptional safety performance, operational excellence, customer satisfaction, workforce development, and profitable growth. This role serves as a key member of the leadership team, translating strategic objectives into operational execution while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and innovation. The role develops leaders, drives operational consistency, and champions the company's values while positioning the organization for long-term success.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Direct supervision of 3-4 managers and provide leadership in support of subordinate managers within a 90+ employee business.

**Hiring Requirements:**

* Four years Technical/Business Administration degree or equivalent, plus extensive (10+ years) experience in the utility industry or equivalent.
* 5+ years of experience in a leadership position responsible for directing and coordinating staff, subcontractors and consultants, and making organizational decisions.
* Excellent financial, business development, customer interaction, and sales skills, with the ability to manage profit and loss responsibilities.
* Thorough understanding of contract administration, specifications, and applicable laws
* Experience in developing strategic plans, leading initiatives, and managing multiple complex priorities to achieve results within demanding timeframes and budgets.
* Excellent writing and presentation, communication (verbal and written) skills required. Computer proficiency with MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* Proven track record of excellent customer service, strong interpersonal skills, problem-solving ability, and the capability to engage with prospective customers at the leadership level.
* OSHA 10 General Industry Certification, or ability to obtain during pre-employment (company provided online training).
* Pass pre-employment drug screen and physical.
* Ability to obtain and maintain a valid unrestricted Driver's License.

For more than 40 years, WhiteWater has been managing, operating, and maintaining municipal and private water and wastewater facilities throughout the northeast with pride and professionalism. We are a subsidiary of R.H. White, an award-winning construction services and solutions company, that has been in business since 1923.

WhiteWater was named 2019 Utility of the Year by the New England Water Works Association and is passionately focused on safely performing great work with our people for our clients. Help us fulfill our mission of protecting public health and (the environment) our most precious natural resource - water.

WhiteWater is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, we encourage all qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

**Regional Director Operations**

**Must Reside in Houston, Austin or San Antonio Area**

**$140,000-$160,000**

**This role is bonus eligible 25% and equity eligible**

**Position Summary**

American Medical Response (AMR) seeks a strategic, results-driven Regional Director of Operations to lead operational excellence, financial performance, and business growth across an assigned region. This leadership position builds a collaborative culture, drives operational excellence, strengthens customer and community partnerships, develops high-performing teams, and ensures quality patient care aligned with organizational objectives. This position oversees 13+ locations and manages multiple direct reports.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight of regional operations to achieve financial, operational, and organizational objectives.
* Drive revenue growth, profitability, market expansion, and business development initiatives.
* Manage budgets, financial forecasts, profit and loss performance, and operational expenses.
* Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, enhance service delivery, and maximize resources.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with healthcare partners, government agencies, community leaders, and key stakeholders.
* Lead, coach, and develop teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure exceptional customer service, contract performance, and long-term client retention.
* Oversee regulatory compliance, safety standards, emergency preparedness, and company policies.
* Partner with regional and corporate leadership to execute strategic initiatives and organizational priorities.
* Support labor relations, workforce planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Champion operational best practices, innovation, and quality patient care.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five years of progressive management experience, including financial oversight and employee leadership.
* Demonstrated success in operational management, strategic planning, and relationship development.
* Healthcare or emergency medical services industry experience is strongly preferred.
* Air Medical Industry experience is highly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, and profit and loss management.
* Proven ability to lead teams, execute strategic initiatives, and deliver measurable business results.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
* Knowledge of healthcare operations, regulatory requirements, and clinical practices preferred.
* Ability to travel approximately 50% within assigned areas as needed.
* Must meet AMR's driving and insurability requirements.

Global Medical Response (GMR) and its family of solutions are dedicated to delivering compassionate, quality medical care, primarily in the areas of emergency and patient relocation services. GMR’s Core Behaviors—keep care at the center, raise your hand, seek to understand, find a way together and be accountable—unite our teams and set us apart in emergency medical services.

About Epirus 

 Epirus is a high-growth technology company developing solid-state, software-defined directed energy systems that enable unprecedented counter-electronics effects and power management solutions to optimize power efficiency in defense and commercial applications. With a constant emphasis on innovation, we are redefining the future of power to bring tomorrow’s capabilities to life, today. And that’s just the beginning. 

 Job Summary 

 Epirus is seeking a strategic, execution-driven Senior Director of Field Operations & Sustainment (FOS) to lead our global customer-facing deployment, support, and validation operations. As a pioneer in software-defined, high-power microwave (HPM) national security solutions—including our flagship Leonidas platform—we are scaling rapidly to support U.S. Department of Defense (DoD), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and international allied customers. 

 High visibility role, reporting into Chief Operating Officer (COO), this role oversees the end-to-end post-manufacturing lifecycle, serving as Epirus’s Deployment Coordinator while leading our five core operational pillars: Field System Readiness & Deployment, Field Service & Technical Operations, Systems Training & Documentation, Global Delivery & Parts Logistics, and Customer Demonstration & Drone Flight Test Operations. You will own full budget development and P&L management for the FOS organization, aligning operational capacity, workforce phasing, and lifecycle supportability with planned sales pipelines and business opportunities.

 Organization & Workforce Management: Set operating priorities, build leadership depth, and phase hiring and qualifications against concurrent program needs. 

 
 
 Budget & Lifecycle Cost Ownership: Develop and manage the full departmental budget based on planned sales and business opportunities. Use field, depot, and support case data to assess reliability, maintainability, spares demand, warranty exposure, and total cost of ownership—feeding findings back into repair, replacement, and redesign decisions. 

 
 
 Demand & Capacity Planning: Balance resources and assets against customer demands and the need to provide live fire demonstrations and exercise operations. Advance site evaluation and planned to ensure successful execution. 

 
 
 Contract Execution & Operational Planning: Support the development of Concepts of Operations (CONOPs) for contracted systems. Represent FOS in weekly contract execution meetings, track readiness and fielding actions, and raise risks that could impact contract milestones. 

 Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner tightly with Engineering, Program Management (PMO), Sales, Business Development, Marketing, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain to ensure seamless execution from production through field sustainment. 

 
 Core Functional Areas 

 
 Field System Readiness & Deployment: 

 
 
 Serve as Epirus’s Deployment Coordinator, owning companywide deployment schedules, personnel and equipment movements, rotations, and redeployment across functional teams. 

 
 
 Oversee post-manufacturing system readiness testing and lead pre-deployment site surveys and reviews with customers prior to shipment to validate site readiness and infrastructure requirements. 

 
 
 Field Service & Technical Operations: 

 
 
 The Field service and technical operations teams are composed of field service technicians and technical operations engineers support all customer repairs, system testing, and on-call customer support, 24/7. They also will manage all service depots and remanufacturing process for component level service. 

 
 
 FSR Management & Scheduling: Manage Field Service Representatives (FSRs) technicians, supporting, scheduling, deployment rotations, customer coverage, and training across CONUS and OCONUS operations.

Overview:

**Hospital Name:** Kessler Institute for Rehabilitation 
**Position:** Director of Plant Operations 
**Location:** Jersey City, NJ

**Compensation**: $90,000 to $145,000 *(Based on years of experience)*

Our inpatient rehabilitation hospital is committed to providing exceptional and compassionate care to best address the medical, physical, emotional, and vocational challenges for individuals with brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, neurological disorders, orthopedic issues, amputation, and multiple traumas.

**We support your career growth and personal well-being:**

* **Start Strong:** Extensive and thorough orientation program to ensure a smooth transition into our setting
* **Your Health Matters**: Comprehensive medical/RX, health, vision, and dental plan offerings
* **Recharge & Refresh:** Generous PTO to maintain a healthy work-life balance
* **Invest in Your Future:** Company-matching 401(k) retirement plan, as well as life and disability protection
* **Your Impact Matters:** Join a team of over 44,000 nationwide committed to providing exceptional care

Responsibilities:

The DPO is a member of the hospital leadership team who works in collaboration with the chief executive officer (CEO) to support the overall operation of the facility, inclusive of administrative and technical operation. Serving as the hospital’s safety officer, the DPO manages the environmental services and security departments to ensure safe operating conditions in compliance with all state, federal and accrediting agencies.

In this role, you are responsible for overseeing all aspects of the maintenance of the facility and grounds, the provision of utilities, the restoration and renovation of the facility and new construction.

* Planning, directing, and supervising all administrative and technical aspects of the department.
* Developing, reviewing, and managing the activities of self and other personnel in the department.
* Actively participating in all hospital committees which impact this department, with specific responsibility on the Safety and Infection Control Committees.
* Establishing and maintaining a Quality Control Program.
* Responsible for maintaining and Environment of Care and OSHA standards in accordance current Federal, State and local standards, guidelines and regulations.

 
Qualifications:

Minimum Requirements:

* Minimum of three (3) years of supervisory experience in provision of maintenance, environmental services, and related services in a hospital environment required.
* Knowledge of JCAHO/OSHA regulations and standards required.

Preferred qualifications that will make you successful:

* College Degree related to building construction and maintenance preferred.

Additional Data:

*Equal Opportunity Employer/including Disabled/Veterans*

* Establish the operating model and talent strategy needed to manage master data end to end.
* Partner with business and technology leaders to align priorities, investments, and capabilities to enterprise objectives.
* Serve as the single point of accountability for master data, translating data strategy into measurable business outcomes.

* Drive standardization and simplification of the master data tooling landscape, rationalizing redundant and legacy tools in favor of common enterprise platforms.

**Director of Practice and ASC Operations**

Reporting to: Chief Operating Officer

**About the Role**

Lead the day-to-day business operations of a multi-provider pain management practice and ambulatory surgery center (ASC). Your initial priorities will be to make it easier for patients and referring offices to reach us, convert more referrals into scheduled visits, and make better use of clinic and procedure capacity.

**A core part of the role is using data, technology, and automation to improve how the practice and ASC operate as they grow.** You’ll use call, referral, and scheduling data to see where patients get stuck and where capacity goes unused. You’ll then redesign workflows, improve how teams use existing systems, and automate repetitive steps such as routing callbacks or flagging referrals that need follow-up. You’ll measure whether those changes improve access, reduce manual work, and free up staff time.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll lead staff, set clear expectations, and work directly with physicians and the ASC Director of Nursing to improve how the practice and surgery center operate. We welcome leaders from healthcare and other complex service businesses. You’ll bring experience leading a team, using data to identify problems, and carrying changes through to measurable results.

**What You Bring**

**Required**

* Progressive operations leadership experience with direct responsibility for hiring, coaching, developing, and managing the performance of a team.
* Experience running a complex, customer-facing operation and managing the drivers of financial performance, such as labor, capacity, productivity, and operating expenses.
* A track record of personally leading workflow improvements that produced measurable, sustained results in access, service, efficiency, or cost.
* Experience using data and KPIs to identify bottlenecks, prioritize action, and verify that changes improved performance.
* Experience using technology or automation to simplify workflows, reduce manual work, and help staff adopt new ways of working.
* Ability to lead changes that span teams, take ownership when progress stalls, and work hands-on with frontline staff to resolve problems.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

**What success looks like**

* **Better patient access.** Make it easier for patients to connect with us and stay engaged throughout their care. Answer more calls live, return messages promptly, and offer convenient online scheduling for eligible visits. Use technology alongside personal outreach to keep patients informed, respond to their needs, and support them throughout their care.
* **Growth and capacity.** Grow completed visits and procedures by strengthening relationships with referring providers, making it easy to refer patients, and keeping referring offices informed. Convert more referrals into completed visits and procedures through timely scheduling, better use of clinic and ASC capacity, and fewer avoidable cancellations.
* **Stronger financial performance.** Labor and supply costs managed to budget, with timely resolution of operational issues affecting collections.
* **Less manual work and clearer accountability.** Use technology and automation to simplify workflows. Set clear ownership for follow-up and use data to track whether changes improve performance and hold over time.

**Preferred**

* Experience in physician practice management, ambulatory surgery, or another regulated service environment.
* Experience coordinating operations across locations or across teams with distinct professional responsibilities.

**Candidates from outside healthcare are encouraged to apply.** Leadership experience and a record of improving operations are essential. Physician practice management experience is optional.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
 
 
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
 
 
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on BESS scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers both standalone BESS facilities and BESS integrated with utility-scale solar PV projects.
 
 
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active BESS construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of BESS Quality across the portfolio.
 
 
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of utility-scale BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, power conversion systems (PCS) and inverters, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary power, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection, suppression, gas detection, and explosion control installation interfaces. Equally important is a working command of manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements, which often govern acceptance more directly than the project drawings. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, battery management and energy management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing remain with Engineering, Commissioning, and the manufacturer; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
 
 
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.

***ABOUT MEITHEAL PHARMACEUTICALS***

*Founded in 2017 and based in Chicago, Meitheal is focused on the development and commercialization of generic injectable medications and, as of 2022, has expanded its focus to include fertility, biologic, and branded products. **Job Summary and Responsibilities**

The Director of Destination Care Operations drives the day-to-day operational success of CommonSpirit Health’s destination care program in partnership with clinical, financial, and internal and external stakeholders – serving patients traveling 150 or more miles for specialty care, from neighboring communities across the United States to international markets. The Director advances program performance, team excellence, and a concierge-caliber patient experience, ensuring every patient experiences frictionless care from first inquiry through return home. This role is suited to a self-driven leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong team leadership, process improvement skills, and comfort leading teams through change. The ideal candidate leads with adaptability, resourcefulness, and a collaborative spirit, and is deeply committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every destination care patient. This is an in-person, onsite role.

* Oversees the day-to-day operational performance of the destination care program, ensuring consistent and high-quality service delivery across all phases of the patient journey. Oversees referral intake and coordination workflows, ensuring timely and accurate routing, follow-up, and communication with referring providers and patients.
* Ensures patients, families, and referring partners experience seamless, concierge-caliber service from initial contact through post-discharge follow-up; conducts regular patient and family rounding to assess experience, identify service gaps and recovery opportunities, reinforce service standards, and gather patient stories that reflect the destination care experience.
* Delivers and ensures culturally informed service, communication, and care coordination across diverse domestic and international patient populations. Partners with clinical leadership and clinical advisory resources to support patient care operations and ensure the clinical needs of the destination care population are addressed. Identifies and leads process improvement and workflow optimization initiatives to advance operational efficiency, service quality, and patient satisfaction; develops and maintains operational protocols and standards that support consistent program delivery.
* Establishes and maintains documentation standards and data integrity practices across the team to support accurate program reporting, operational decision-making, and continuity of patient care. Serves as the escalation point for the team and provides availability for complex or time-sensitive situations as they arise. Manages the destination care program budget and is accountable for financial performance against established targets.
* Sets clear performance expectations, invests in professional growth, and builds and sustains a high-performing team culture grounded in service excellence, operational consistency, and continuous improvement; establishes clear standards and ensures consistent adherence across the team, addressing performance gaps directly and constructively.
* Oversees onboarding, cross-training, and workflow consistency across the program. Leads change management efforts within the team to support adoption of new workflows, service standards, and program initiatives.

* Experience managing and developing teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare organization, with direct accountability for program performance outcomes, upon hire and
* Experience delivering high-touch, patient-centered services for complex or high-acuity patient populations, including programs such as transplant, oncology, specialty referral, or equivalent tertiary or quaternary care settings, upon hire and

***Job Title: Director, Manufacturing Engineering***
***Job Code: 47622***
***Job Location: Camden, AR***
***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***
**Job Description:**
The Manufacturing Engineering Director in Camden, Arkansas will plan, organize and technically direct the manufacturing engineering activities and staff. Enable Operations to execute all programs in a safe and efficient manner, and ensuring the achievement of quality, cost and delivery schedule objectives. This position reports to the Senior Director Operations and Site Management. Our Camden, AR site is at $600M+ revenue and produces a diverse portfolio of highly engineered products for aerospace and defense applications. The individual will be responsible for implementing a disciplined operating system in line with the enterprise while improving the operating effectiveness of the site and leading an organization of over 190 people.
 
 
**Essential Functions:**

* 50% - Direct and lead technical team: Analyze, evaluate and determine appropriate solutions for manufacturing technical problems encountered in the application of manufacturing methods, facilities and processes. Apply engineering procedures, provide technical direction, create and apply work instructions and tooling for the factory floor. Participate in program and site corrective action boards and be a key member in customer escape and non-conformance investigations; develop direct cause, root cause and mistake proof corrective actions, as well as separation criteria when required. Ensure proper deployment of resources to achieve cost effective results in support of site and business unit deliverables. Direct the installation of Electronic Work Instructions (Platform is DELMIA) across the site and all product lines. Strict oversight of the Job Safety Analysis and Process Safety Management programs at the site.
* 15% - Administrative management: Ensure a safe work environment and remain in compliance to federal and local regulations. Develop long range technical and administrative plans, goals and strategies.
* 15% - Customer interface: Establish priorities to meet the needs of the customer and the organization with a dedication to support the manufacturing shop floor. Represent the organization as a prime internal and customer contact on manufacturing technical operations.
* 20% - Strategy and Continuous Improvement: Lead the sites Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) program. Drive operational

excellence throughout the organization and create a metrics driven, highly accountable mindset within the organization.
 
 

* Ability to obtain a US secret security clearance.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of 15 years prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree with a minimum of 13 years prior relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 19 years of prior relevant experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Demonstrated supervisory and leadership skills, including planning, organizing and directing activities; developing talent; and collaborating across business units and functional teams to achieve site objectives.
* Strong understanding of business development, program management, engineering, finance, operations

-----------------------------

This position serves as the senior strategic people leader and trusted advisor to the SVP – U.S. General Manager and the U.S. Executive Leadership Team, overseeing HR for U.S. Field Sales, U.S. Marketing, and U.S. Manufacturing (approximately 950 employees). * Assess the effectiveness of the organization’s business model and dynamics, and lead realignment as needed to drive performance
